title: Psalms 132:5
text: 5. habitation--literally, "dwellings," generally used to denote the sanctuary.

title: Psalms 132:6
text:
6. These may be the "words of David" and his pious friends, who, 
 
    at Ephratah--or Beth-lehem ( Genesis 48:7 ), where he once lived, may have heard of the ark, which he found for the first time 
 
    in the fields of the wood--or, Jair, or Kirjath-jearim ("City of woods") ( I Samuel 7:1 II Samuel 6:3 II Samuel 6:4 ), whence it was brought to Zion.

title: Psalms 132:7
text: 7. The purpose of engaging in God's worship is avowed.

title: Psalms 132:8
text: 8, 9. The solemn entry of the ark, symbolical of God's presence and power, with the attending priests, into the sanctuary, is proclaimed in the words used by Solomon ( II Chronicles 6:41 ).

title: Psalms 132:10
text:
10-12. For thy servant David's sake--that is, On account of the promise made to him. 
 
    turn ... anointed--Repulse not him who, as David's descendant, pleads the promise to perpetuate his royal line. After reciting the promise, substantially from  II Samuel 7:12-16  (compare  Acts 2:30 , &c.), an additional plea,

title: Psalms 132:13
text: 13. is made on the ground of God's choice of Zion (here used for Jerusalem) as His dwelling, inasmuch as the prosperity of the kingdom was connected with that of the Church ( Psalms 122:8 Psalms 122:9 ).

title: Psalms 132:14
text: 14-18. That choice is expressed in God's words, "I will sit" or "dwell," or sit enthroned The joy of the people springs from the blessings of His grace, conferred through the medium of the priesthood.

title: Psalms 132:17
text:
17. make the horn ... to bud--enlarge his power. 
 
    a lamp--the figure of prosperity ( Psalms 18:10 Psalms 18:28 Psalms 89:17 ). With the confounding of his enemies is united his prosperity and the unceasing splendor of his crown.

title: Psalms 133:1
text:
Psalms 133:1-3 . The blessings of fraternal unity. 
 
    1, 2. As the fragrant oil is refreshing, so this affords delight. The holy anointing oil for the high priest was olive oil mixed with four of the best spices ( Exodus 30:22 Exodus 30:25 Exodus 30:30 ). Its rich profusion typified the abundance of the Spirit's graces. As the copious dew, such as fell on Hermon, falls in fertilizing power on the mountains of Zion, so this unity is fruitful in good works.

title: Psalms 133:3
text:
3. there--that is, in Zion, the Church; the material Zion, blessed with enriching dews, suggests this allusion the source of the influence enjoyed by the spiritual Zion. 
 
    commanded the blessing--(Compare  Psalms 68:28 ).

title: Psalms 134:1
text:
Psalms 134:1-3 . 1, 2. The pilgrim bands arriving at the sanctuary call on the priests, who 
 
    stand in the house of the Lord--at the time of the evening sacrifice, to unite in praising God in their name and that of the people, using appropriate gestures, to which the priests reply, pronouncing the Mosaic blessing which they alone could pronounce. A fit epilogue to the whole pilgrim-book, Psalms 120-134. 
 
    by night--the evening service ( Psalms 141:2 ), as opposed to morning ( Psalms 92:2 ).

title: Psalms 134:2
text: 2. Lift up your hands--(Compare  Psalms 28:2 ).

title: Psalms 134:3
text:
3. After the manner directed ( Numbers 6:23 ). 
 
    out of Zion--the Church, as His residence, and thus seat of blessings. Thus close the songs of degrees.

title: Psalms 135:1
text:
Psalms 135:1-21 . A Psalm of praise, in which God's relations to His Church, His power in the natural world, and in delivering His people, are contrasted with the vanity of idols and idol-worship. 
 
    1-3. In the general call for praise, the priests, that stand in the house of the Lord, are specially mentioned.

title: Psalms 135:4
text: 4-7. God's choice of Israel is the first reason assigned for rendering praise; the next, His manifested greatness in creation and providence.

title: Psalms 135:6
text: 6. heaven, and ... seas, and all ... ends of the earth--denote universality.

title: Psalms 135:8
text: 8, 9. The last plague [ Exodus 12:29 ] is cited to illustrate His "tokens and wonders."

title: Psalms 135:10
text: 10-12. The conquest of Canaan was by God's power, not that of the people.

title: Psalms 135:13
text:
13. heritage--or, "possession." 
 
    name ... memorial--Each denote that by which God is made known.

title: Psalms 135:14
text:
14. will judge--do justice ( Psalms 72:2 ). 
 
    repent himself--change His dealings ( Psalms 90:13 ).

title: Psalms 135:15
text: 15-18. (Compare  Psalms 115:4-8 ).

title: Psalms 135:18
text: 18. are like unto them--or, "shall be like," &c. Idolaters become spiritually stupid and perish with their idols ( Isaiah 1:31 ).

title: Psalms 135:19
text: 19-21. (Compare  Psalms 115:9-11 ). There we have "trust" for "bless" here.

title: Psalms 135:21
text: 21. out of Zion--(Compare  Psalms 110:2 Psalms 134:3 ). From the Church, as a center, His praise is diffused throughout the earth.

title: Psalms 136:1
text:
Psalms 136:1-26 . The theme is the same as that of Psalm 135. God should be praised for His works of creation and providence, His deliverance and care of His people, and judgments on their enemies, and His goodness to all. The chorus to every verse is in terms of that of  Psalms 106:1 Psalms 118:1-4 , and was perhaps used as the Amen by the people, in worship (compare  I Chronicles 16:36 Psalms 105:45 ). 
 
    1-3. The divine titles denote supremacy.

title: Psalms 136:4
text: 4. alone--excluding all help.

title: Psalms 136:5
text:
5, 6. by wisdom--or, "in wisdom" ( Psalms 104:24 ). 
 
    made--literally, "maker of." 
 
    above the waters--or, "higher than the waters" ( Psalms 24:2 ).

title: Psalms 136:12
text: 12. Compare similar expressions ( Exodus 3:20 Deuteronomy 4:34 , &c.).

title: Psalms 136:15
text: 15. overthrew--literally, "shook off," as in  Exodus 14:27 , as a contemptuous rejection of a reptile.

title: Psalms 136:23
text:
23. remembered us--or, "for us" ( Psalms 132:1 ). 
 
    our low estate--that is, captivity.

title: Psalms 136:24
text: 24. And hath redeemed us--or, literally, "snatched us"--alluding to the sudden deliverance effected by the overthrow of Babylon.

title: Psalms 136:25
text: 25. To the special favors to His people is added the record of God's goodness to all His creatures (compare  Matthew 6:30 ).

title: Psalms 136:26
text: 26. God of heaven--occurs but once ( Jonah 1:9 ) before the captivity.  It is used by the later writers as specially distinguishing God from idols.

title: Psalms 137:1
text:
Psalms 137:1-9 . This Psalm records the mourning of the captive Israelites, and a prayer and prediction respecting the destruction of their enemies. 
 
    1. rivers of Babylon--the name of the city used for the whole country. 
 
    remembered Zion--or, Jerusalem, as in  Psalms 132:13 .

title: Psalms 137:2
text: 2. upon the willows--which may have grown there then, if not now; as the palm, which was once common, is now rare in Palestine.

title: Psalms 137:3
text: 3, 4. Whether the request was in curiosity or derision, the answer intimates that a compliance was incongruous with their mournful feelings ( Proverbs 25:20 ).

title: Psalms 137:5
text: 5, 6. For joyful songs would imply forgetfulness of their desolated homes and fallen Church. The solemn imprecations on the hand and tongue, if thus forgetful, relate to the cunning or skill in playing, and the power of singing.

title: Psalms 137:7
text:
7-9. Remember ... the children of Edom--(Compare  Psalms 132:1 ), that is, to punish. 
 
    the day of Jerusalem--its downfall ( Lamentations 4:21 Lamentations 4:22 Obadiah 1:21 ).

title: Psalms 137:8
text: 8. daughter of Babylon--the people ( Psalms 9:13 ). Their destruction had been abundantly foretold ( Isaiah 13:14 Jeremiah 51:23 ). For the terribleness of that destruction, God's righteous judgment, and not the passions of the chafed Israelites, was responsible.

title: Psalms 138:1
text:
Psalms 138:1-8 . David thanks God for His benefits, and anticipating a wider extension of God's glory by His means, assures himself of His continued presence and faithfulness. 
 
    1. I will praise thee with my whole heart--(Compare  Psalms 9:1 ). 
 
    before the gods--whether angels ( Psalms 8:5 ); or princes ( Exodus 21:6 Psalms 82:6 ); or idols ( Psalms 97:7 ); denotes a readiness to worship the true God alone, and a contempt of all other objects of worship.

title: Psalms 138:2
text:
2. (Compare  Psalms 5:7 ). 
 
    thy word above all thy name--that is, God's promise ( II Samuel 7:12-16 ), sustained by His mercy and truth, exceeded all other manifestations of Himself as subject of praise.

title: Psalms 138:3
text: 3-5. That promise, as an answer to his prayers in distress, revived and strengthened his faith; and, as the basis of other revelations of the Messiah, it will be the occasion of praise by all who hear and receive it ( Psalms 68:29 Psalms 68:31 Isaiah 4:3 ).

title: Psalms 138:5
text: 5. for great is the glory--or, "when the glory shall be great," in God's fulfilling His purposes of redemption.

title: Psalms 138:6
text:
6, 7. On this general principle of God's government ( Isaiah 2:11 Isaiah 57:15 Isaiah 66:2 ), he relies for God's favor in saving him, and overthrowing his enemies. 
 
    knoweth afar off--their ways and deserts ( Psalms 1:6 ).

title: Psalms 138:8
text: 8. God will fulfil His promise.

title: Psalms 139:1
text: Psalms 139:1-24 . After presenting the sublime doctrines of God's omnipresence and omniscience, the Psalmist appeals to Him, avowing his innocence, his abhorrence of the wicked, and his ready submission to the closest scrutiny. Admonition to the wicked and comfort to the pious are alike implied inferences from these doctrines.

title: Psalms 140:1
text:
Psalms 140:1-13 . The style of this Psalm resembles those of David in the former part of the book, presenting the usual complaint, prayer, and confident hope of relief. 
 
    1. evil man--Which of David's enemies is meant is not important.

title: Psalms 140:2
text: 2-5. This character of the wicked, and the devices planned against the pious, correspond to  Psalms 10:7 Psalms 31:13 Psalms 58:4 , &c.

title: Psalms 140:3
text: 3. sharpened ... like a serpent--not like a serpent does, but they are thus like a serpent in cunning and venom.

title: Psalms 140:5
text: 5. snare [and] net--for threatening dangers (compare  Psalms 38:12 Psalms 57:6 ).

title: Psalms 140:6
text: 6. (Compare  Psalms 5:1-12 Psalms 16:2 ).

title: Psalms 140:7
text: 7. day of battle--literally, "of armor," that is, when using it.

title: Psalms 140:8
text:
8. (Compare  Psalms 37:12 Psalms 66:7 ). 
 
    lest they exalt themselves--or, they will be exalted if permitted to prosper.

title: Psalms 140:9
text: 9. Contrasts his head covered by God ( Psalms 140:7 ) with theirs, or (as "head" may be used for "persons") with them, covered with the results of their wicked deeds ( Psalms 7:16 ).

title: Psalms 140:10
text:
10. (Compare  Psalms 11:6 Psalms 120:4 ). 
 
    cast into the fire; into deep pits--figures for utter destruction.

title: Psalms 140:11
text: 11. an evil speaker--or, "slanderer" will not be tolerated ( Psalms 101:7 ). The last clause may be translated: "an evil (man) He (God) shall hunt," &c.

title: Psalms 140:12
text: 12. (Compare  Psalms 9:4 ).

title: Psalms 140:13
text:
13. After all changes, the righteous shall have cause for praise. Such 
 
    shall dwell--shall sit securely, under God's protection ( Psalms 21:6 Psalms 41:12 ).

title: Psalms 141:1
text: Psalms 141:1-10 . This Psalm evinces its authorship as the preceding, by its structure and the character of its contents. It is a prayer for deliverance from sins to which affliction tempted him, and from the enemies who caused it.

title: Psalms 142:1
text:
Psalms 142:1-7 . Maschil--(See on  Psalms 31:24 , title).  When he was in the cave--either of Adullam ( I Samuel 22:1 ), or En-gedi ( I Samuel 24:3 ). This does not mean that the Psalm was composed in the cave, but that the precarious mode of life, of which his refuge in caves was a striking illustration, occasioned the complaint, which constitutes the first part of the Psalm and furnishes the reason for the prayer with which it concludes, and which, as the prominent characteristic, gives its name. 
 
    1. with my voice--audibly, because earnestly.

title: Psalms 142:2
text:
2. (Compare  Psalms 62:8 ). 
 
    I poured out my complaint--or, "a sad musing."

title: Psalms 142:3
text: 3. thou knewest ... path--The appeal is indicative of conscious innocence; knowest it to be right, and that my affliction is owing to the snares of enemies, and is not deserved (compare  Psalms 42:4 Psalms 61:2 ).

title: Psalms 142:4
text:
4. Utter desolation is meant. 
 
    right hand--the place of a protector ( Psalms 110:5 ). 
 
    cared for--literally, "sought after," to do good.

title: Psalms 142:5
text: 5. (Compare  Psalms 31:14 Psalms 62:7 ).

title: Psalms 142:6
text: 6. (Compare  Psalms 17:1 ).

title: Psalms 142:7
text:
7. (Compare  Psalms 25:17 ). 
 
    that I may praise--literally, "for praising," or, "that Thy name may be praised," that is, by the righteous, who shall surround me with sympathizing joy ( Psalms 35:27 ).

title: Psalms 143:1
text:
Psalms 143:1-12 . In structure and style, like the preceding (Psalms 104-142), this Psalm is clearly evinced to be David's. It is a prayer for pardon, and for relief from enemies; afflictions, as usual, producing confession and penitence. 
 
    1. in thy faithfulness ... and ... righteousness--or, God's regard to the claims which He has permitted His people to make in His covenant.

title: Psalms 143:2
text:
2. enter ... judgment--deal not in strict justice. 
 
    shall no ... justified--or, "is no man justified," or "innocent" ( Job 14:3 Romans 3:20 ).

title: Psalms 143:3
text:
3, 4. The exciting reason for his prayer--his afflictions--led to confession as just made: he now makes the complaint. 
 
    as those that have been long dead--deprived of life's comforts (compare  Psalms 40:15 Psalms 88:3-6 ).

title: Psalms 143:5
text:
5, 6. The distress is aggravated by the contrast of former comfort ( Psalms 22:3-5 ), for whose return he longs. 
 
    a thirsty land--which needs rain, as did his spirit God's gracious visits ( Psalms 28:1 Psalms 89:17 ).

title: Psalms 143:7
text: 7. spirit faileth--is exhausted.

title: Psalms 143:8
text:
8. (Compare  Psalms 25:1-4 Psalms 59:16 ). 
 
    the way ... walk--that is, the way of safety and righteousness ( Psalms 142:3-6 ).

title: Psalms 143:9
text: 9. (Compare  Psalms 31:15-20 ).

title: Psalms 143:10
text:
10. (Compare  Psalms 5:8 Psalms 27:11 ). 
 
    land of uprightness--literally, "an even land" ( Psalms 26:12 ).

title: Psalms 143:11
text: 11. (Compare  Psalms 23:3 Psalms 119:156 ).

title: Psalms 143:12
text:
12. God's mercy to His people is often wrath to His and their enemies (compare  Psalms 31:17 ). 
 
    thy servant--as chosen to be such, entitled to divine regard.

title: Psalms 144:1
text: Psalms 144:1-15 . David's praise of God as his all-sufficient help is enhanced by a recognition of the intrinsic worthlessness of man. Confidently imploring God's interposition against his enemies, he breaks forth into praise and joyful anticipations of the prosperity of his kingdom, when freed from vain and wicked men.

title: Psalms 145:1
text:
Psalms 145:1-21 . A Psalm of praise to God for His mighty, righteous, and gracious government of all men, and of His humble and suffering people in particular. 
 
    1, 2. (Compare  Psalms 30:1 ). 
 
    bless thy name--celebrate Thy perfections ( Psalms 5:11 ). God is addressed as king, alluding to His government of men.

title: Psalms 145:3
text:
3. (Compare  Psalms 18:3 Psalms 48:1 ). 
 
    greatness--as displayed in His works.

title: Psalms 145:4
text: 4. shall declare--literally, "they shall declare," that is all generations.

title: Psalms 145:5
text:
5. I will speak--or, "muse" ( Psalms 77:12 Psalms 119:15 ). 
 
    thy wondrous works--or, "words of thy wonders," that is, which described them ( Psalms 105:27 , Margin).

title: Psalms 145:6
text: 6. terrible acts--which produce dread or fear.

title: Psalms 145:7
text:
7. memory-- ( Psalms 6:5 ), remembrance, or what causes to be remembered. 
 
    righteousness--as in  Psalms 143:1 , goodness according to covenant engagement.

title: Psalms 145:8
text:
8, 9. (Compare  Psalms 103:8 Psalms 111:4 ). 
 
    over all, &c.--rests on all His works.

title: Psalms 145:10
text: 10. bless--as in  Psalms 145:1 , to praise with reverence, more than merely to praise.

title: Psalms 145:11
text: 11, 12. The declaration of God's glory is for the extension of His knowledge and perfections in the world.

title: Psalms 145:13
text: 13. (Compare  Daniel 4:3 Daniel 4:34 ).

title: Psalms 145:14
text: 14. (Compare  Psalms 37:17 Psalms 54:4 ).

title: Psalms 145:15
text: 15, 16. eyes of ... thee--or, look with expecting faith ( Psalms 104:27 Psalms 104:28 ).

title: Psalms 145:17
text:
17. holy ... works--literally, "merciful" or "kind, goodness" ( Psalms 144:2 ) is the corresponding noun. 
 
    righteous--in a similar relation of meaning to "righteousness" ( Psalms 145:7 ).

title: Psalms 145:18
text: 18, 19. (Compare  Psalms 34:7 Psalms 34:10 ).

title: Psalms 145:20
text: 20. Those who fear Him ( Psalms 145:19 ) are those who are here said to love Him.

title: Psalms 145:21
text:
21. (Compare  Psalms 33:21 ). 
 
    all flesh-- ( Psalms 65:2 ). The Psalm ends, as it began, with ascriptions of praise, in which the pious will ever delight to join.

title: Psalms 146:1
text: Psalms 146:1-10 . An exhortation to praise God, who, by the gracious and faithful exercise of His power in goodness to the needy, is alone worthy of implicit trust.

title: Psalms 147:1
text:
Psalms 147:1-20 . This and the remaining Psalms have been represented as specially designed to celebrate the rebuilding of Jerusalem (compare  Nehemiah 6:16 Nehemiah 12:27 ). They all open and close with the stirring call for praise. This one specially declares God's providential care towards all creatures, and particularly His people. 
 
    1. (Compare  Psalms 92:1 Psalms 135:3 ).

title: Psalms 147:2
text: 2. (Compare  Psalms 107:3 Isaiah 11:12 ).

title: Psalms 147:3
text:
3. Though applicable to the captive Israelites, this is a general and precious truth. 
 
    wounds--(Compare Margin).

title: Psalms 147:4
text:
4, 5. God's power in nature ( Isaiah 40:26-28 ), and often) is presented as a pledge of His power to help His people. 
 
    telleth ... stars--what no man can do ( Genesis 15:5 ).

title: Psalms 147:6
text: 6. That power is put forth for the good of the meek and suffering pious, and confusion of the wicked ( Psalms 146:8 Psalms 146:9 ).

title: Psalms 147:7
text:
7-9. His providence supplies bountifully the wild animals in their mountain homes. 
 
    Sing ... Lord--literally, "Answer the Lord," that is, in grateful praise to His goodness, thus declared in His acts.

title: Psalms 147:10
text: 10, 11. The advantages afforded, as in war by the strength of the horse or the agility of man, do not incline God to favor any; but those who fear and, of course, trust Him, will obtain His approbation and aid.

title: Psalms 147:13
text: 13. strengthened ... gates--or, means of defense against invaders,

title: Psalms 147:14
text:
14. maketh ... borders--or, territories ( Genesis 23:17 Isaiah 54:12 ). 
 
    filleth thee, &c.--(Compare Margin).

title: Psalms 147:15
text: 15-18. God's Word, as a swift messenger, executes His purpose, for with Him to command is to perform ( Genesis 1:3 Psalms 33:9 ), and He brings about the wonders of providence as easily as men cast crumbs.

title: Psalms 147:17
text: 17. morsels--used as to food ( Genesis 18:5 ), perhaps here denotes hail.

title: Psalms 147:19
text: 19, 20. This mighty ruler and benefactor of heaven and earth is such especially to His chosen people, to whom alone ( Deuteronomy 4:32-34 ) He has made known His will, while others have been left in darkness. Therefore unite in the great hallelujah.

title: Psalms 148:1
text:
Psalms 148:1-14 . The scope of this Psalm is the same as that of the preceding. 
 
    1. heavens [and] heights--are synonymous.

title: Psalms 148:2
text: 2. hosts--(compare  Psalms 103:21 ).

title: Psalms 148:4
text:
4. heavens of heavens--the very highest. 
 
    waters--clouds, resting above the visible heavens (compare  Genesis 1:7 ).

title: Psalms 148:5
text:
5. praise the name--as representing His perfections. 
 
    he commanded--"He" is emphatic, ascribing creation to God alone.

title: Psalms 148:6
text:
6. The perpetuity of the frame of nature is, of course, subject to Him who formed it. 
 
    a decree ... pass--His ordinances respecting them shall not change ( Jeremiah 36:31 ), or perish ( Job 34:20 Psalms 37:36 ).

title: Psalms 148:7
text: 7-10. The call on the earth, as opposed to heaven, includes seas or depths, whose inhabitants the dragon, as one of the largest (on leviathan, see on  Psalms 104:25 ), is selected to represent. The most destructive and ungovernable agents of inanimate nature are introduced

title: Psalms 148:8
text: 8. fulfilling his word--or, law, may be understood of each. Next the most distinguished productions of the vegetable world.

title: Psalms 148:9
text: 9. fruitful trees--or, "trees of fruit," as opposed to forest trees. Wild and domestic, large and small animals are comprehended.

title: Psalms 148:11
text:
11, 12. Next all rational beings, from the highest in rank to little children. 
 
    princes--or, military leaders.

title: Psalms 148:13
text:
13. Let them--all mentioned. 
 
    excellent--or, exalted ( Isaiah 12:4 ). 
 
    his glory--majesty ( Psalms 45:3 ). 
 
    above the earth and heaven--Their united splendors fail to match His.

title: Psalms 148:14
text:
14. exalteth the horn--established power ( Psalms 75:5 Psalms 75:6 ). 
 
    praise of--or literally, "for" 
 
    his saints--that is, occasions for them to praise Him. They are further described as "His people," and "near unto Him," sustaining by covenanted care a peculiarly intimate relation.

title: Psalms 149:1
text:
Psalms 149:1-9 . This Psalm sustains a close connection with the foregoing. The chosen people are exhorted to praise God, in view of past favors, and also future victories over enemies, of which they are impliedly assured. 
 
    1. (Compare  Psalms 96:1 ).

title: Psalms 149:2
text: 2. God had signalized His relation as a sovereign, in restoring them to their land.

title: Psalms 149:3
text:
3. in the dance-- ( Psalms 30:11 ). The dance is connected with other terms, expressive of the great joy of the occasion. The word may be rendered "lute," to which the other instruments are joined. 
 
    sing praises--or, sing and play.

title: Psalms 149:4
text:
4. taketh pleasure--literally, "accepts," alluding to acceptance of propitiatory offerings (compare  Psalms 147:11 ). 
 
    beautify, &c.--adorn the humble with faith, hope, joy, and peace.

title: Psalms 149:5
text:
5. in glory--the honorable condition to which they are raised. 
 
    upon their beds--once a place of mourning ( Psalms 6:6 ).

title: Psalms 149:6
text: 6. high praises--or, "deeds." They shall go forth as religious warriors, as once religious laborers ( Nehemiah 4:17 ).

title: Psalms 149:7
text: 7. The destruction of the incorrigibly wicked attends the propagation of God's truth, so that the military successes of the Jews, after the captivity, typified the triumphs of the Gospel.

title: Psalms 149:9
text:
9. the judgment written--either in God's decrees, or perhaps as in  Deuteronomy 32:41-43 . 
 
    this honour--that is, to be thus employed, will be an honorable service, to be assigned 
 
    his saints--or, godly ones ( Psalms 16:3 ).

title: Psalms 150:1
text:
Psalms 150:1-6 . This is a suitable doxology for the whole book, reciting the "place, theme, mode, and extent of God's high praise." 
 
    1. in his sanctuary--on earth. 
 
    firmament of his power--which illustrates His power.

title: Psalms 150:2
text:
2. mighty acts-- ( Psalms 145:4 ). 
 
    excellent greatness--or, abundance of greatness.

title: Psalms 150:3
text: 3, 4. trumpet--used to call religious assemblies;

title: Psalms 150:4
text: 4. organs--or pipe, a wind instrument, and the others were used in worship.

title: Psalms 150:5
text: 5. cymbals--suited to loud praise ( Nehemiah 12:27 ).

title: Psalms 150:6
text: 6. LIVING VOICES SHALL TAKE UP THE FAILING SOUNDS OF DEAD INSTRUMENTS, AND AS THEY CEASE ON EARTH, THOSE OF INTELLIGENT RANSOMED SPIRITS AND HOLY ANGELS, AS WITH THE SOUND OF MIGHTY THUNDERS, WILL PROLONG ETERNALLY THE PRAISE, SAYING: "ALLELUIA! SALVATION, AND GLORY, AND HONOR, AND POWER, UNTO THE LORD OUR GOD"; ALLELUIA! FOR THE LORD GOD OMNIPOTENT REIGNETH." AMEN!

title: Proverbs 1:1
text:
Proverbs 1:1-33 . After the title the writer defines the design and nature of the instructions of the book. He paternally invites attention to those instructions and warns his readers against the enticements of the wicked. In a beautiful personification, wisdom is then introduced in a most solemn and impressive manner, publicly inviting men to receive its teachings, warning those who reject, and encouraging those who accept, the proffered instructions. 
 
    1-4. (See (unresolved link) Part I).

title: Proverbs 1:2
text:
2. To know ... instruction--literally, "for knowing," that is, such is the design of these writings. 
 
    wisdom--or the use of the best means for the best ends, is generally employed in this book for true piety. 
 
    instruction--discipline, by which men are trained. 
 
    to perceive--literally, "for perceiving," the design (as above) 
 
    understanding--that is, words which enable one to discern good and evil.

title: Proverbs 1:3
text:
3. To receive ... of wisdom--For receiving that discipline which discretion imparts. The Hebrew for "wisdom" differs from that of  Proverbs 1:2 , and denotes rather discreet counsel. Compare the opposite traits of the fool ( Proverbs 16:22 ). 
 
    justice ... equity--all the attributes of one upright in all his relations to God and man.

title: Proverbs 1:4
text:
4. simple--one easily led to good or evil; so the parallel. 
 
    young man--one inexperienced. 
 
    subtilty--or prudence ( Proverbs 3:21 Proverbs 5:21 ). 
 
    discretion--literally, "device," both qualities, either good or bad, according to their use. Here good, as they imply wariness by which to escape evil and find good.

title: Proverbs 1:5
text:
5, 6. Such writings the wise, who pursue right ends by right means, will value. 
 
    learning--not the act, but matter of it. 
 
    wise counsels--or the art and principles of governing.

title: Proverbs 1:6
text:
6. To understand--so as to ... such will be the result. 
 
    interpretation--(Compare Margin). 
 
    words of the wise--(Compare  Proverbs 1:2 ). 
 
    dark sayings--(Compare  Psalms 49:4 John 16:25 ; and see (unresolved link), Part I).

title: Proverbs 1:7
text:
7. The fear of the Lord--the principle of true piety (compare  Proverbs 2:5 Proverbs 14:26 Proverbs 14:27 Job 28:28 Psalms 34:11 Psalms 111:10 Acts 9:31 ). 
 
    beginning--first part, foundation. 
 
    fools--the stupid and indifferent to God's character and government; hence the wicked.

title: Proverbs 1:8
text: 8. My son--This paternal form denotes a tender regard for the reader. Filial sentiments rank next to piety towards God, and ensure most distinguished rewards (compare  Proverbs 6:20 Ephesians 6:2 Ephesians 6:3 ).

title: Proverbs 1:9
text: 9. On the figures of  Proverbs 1:9 , compare  Genesis 41:42 Song of Solomon 1:10 Song of Solomon 4:9 .

title: Proverbs 1:10
text:
10-19. A solemn warning against temptation. 
 
    entice--literally, "open the way." 
 
    consent ... not--Sin is in consenting or yielding to temptation, not in being tempted.

title: Proverbs 1:11
text:
11-14. Murder and robbery are given as specific illustrations. 
 
    lay wait ... lurk privily--express an effort and hope for successful concealment. 
 
    swallow ... grave--utterly destroy the victim and traces of the crime ( Numbers 16:33 Psalms 55:15 ). Abundant rewards of villainy are promised as the fruits of this easy and safe course.

title: Proverbs 1:15
text: 15, 16. The society of the wicked (way or path) is dangerous. Avoid the beginnings of sin ( Proverbs 4:14 Psalms 1:1 Psalms 119:101 ).

title: Proverbs 1:17
text: 17-19. Men warned ought to escape danger as birds instinctively avoid visibly spread nets. But stupid sinners rush to their own ruin ( Psalms 9:16 ), and, greedy of gain, succeed in the very schemes which destroy them ( I Timothy 6:10 ), not only failing to catch others, but procuring their own destruction.

title: Proverbs 1:20
text:
20-33. Some interpreters regard this address as the language of the Son of God under the name of Wisdom (compare  Luke 11:49 ). Others think that wisdom, as the divine attribute specially employed in acts of counsel and admonition, is here personified, and represents God. In either case the address is a most solemn and divine admonition, whose matter and spirit are eminently evangelical and impressive (see on  Proverbs 7:27 ). 
 
    Wisdom--literally, "Wisdoms," the plural used either because of the unusual sense, or as indicative of the great excellency of wisdom (compare  Proverbs 9:1 ). 
 
    streets--or most public places, not secretly.

title: Proverbs 1:21
text: 21. The publicity further indicated by terms designating places of most common resort.

title: Proverbs 1:22
text:
22. simple ones--(Compare  Proverbs 1:4 ). 
 
    simplicity--implying ignorance. 
 
    scorners-- ( Psalms 1:1 ) --who despise, as well as reject, truth. 
 
    fools--Though a different word is used from that of  Proverbs 1:7 , yet it is of the same meaning.

title: Proverbs 1:23
text:
23. reproof--implying conviction deserving it (compare  John 16:8 , Margin). 
 
    pour out--abundantly impart. 
 
    my spirit--whether of wisdom personified, or of Christ, a divine agent.

title: Proverbs 1:24
text: 24. stretched ... hand--Earnestness, especially in beseeching, is denoted by the figure (compare  Job 11:13 Psalms 68:31 Psalms 88:9 ).

title: Proverbs 1:25
text:
25. set at naught--rejected as of no value. 
 
    would none of--literally, "were not willing or inclined to it."

title: Proverbs 1:26
text: 26, 27. In their extreme distress He will not only refuse help, but aggravate it by derision.

title: Proverbs 1:27
text:
27. fear--the object of it. 
 
    desolation--literally, "a tumultuous noise," denoting their utter confusion. 
 
    destruction--or calamity ( Proverbs 1:26 ) compared to a whirlwind, as to fatal rapidity. 
 
    distress-- ( Psalms 4:1 Psalms 44:11 ). 
 
    anguish--a state of inextricable oppression, the deepest despair.

title: Proverbs 1:28
text: 28. Now no prayers or most diligent seeking will avail ( Proverbs 8:17 ).

title: Proverbs 1:29
text: 29, 30. The sinner's infatuated rejection brings his ruin.

title: Proverbs 1:31
text:
31. fruit ... way--result of conduct ( Isaiah 3:10 Ezekiel 11:21 Romans 6:21 Galatians 6:7 Galatians 6:8 ). 
 
    be filled--even to repletion ( Psalms 123:4 ).

title: Proverbs 1:32
text:
32. turning away--that is, from the call of  Proverbs 1:23 . 
 
    simple--as in  Proverbs 1:22 . 
 
    prosperity--quiet, implying indifference.

title: Proverbs 1:33
text:
33. dwell safely--literally, "in confidence" ( Deuteronomy 12:10 ). 
 
    be quiet--or at ease, in real prosperity. 
 
    from fear--without fear.

title: Proverbs 2:1
text:
Proverbs 2:1-22 . Men are invited to seek wisdom because it teaches those principles by which they may obtain God's guidance and avoid the society and influence of the wicked, whose pernicious courses are described. 
 
    1-5. Diligence in hearing and praying for instruction must be used to secure the great principle of godliness, the fear of God. 
 
    hide ... with thee--lay up in store (compare  Proverbs 7:1 ).

title: Proverbs 2:2
text:
2. Listen attentively and reflect seriously ( Proverbs 1:24 Psalms 130:2 ). 
 
    understanding--right perception of truth.

title: Proverbs 2:3
text:
3. Yea, if--literally, "When if," that is, in such a case. 
 
    knowledge--or, "discrimination." 
 
    understanding--as in  Proverbs 2:2 .

title: Proverbs 2:4
text: 4. There must be earnest prayer and effort.

title: Proverbs 2:5
text:
5. understand--or, "perceive intelligently." 
 
    find--obtain.

title: Proverbs 2:6
text:
6. For--God is ready ( James 1:5 James 4:8 ). 
 
    out of his mouth--by revelation from Him.

title: Proverbs 2:7
text:
7. sound wisdom--literally, "substance," opposed to what is fictitious.  According to the context, this may be assistance, as here corresponding with 
 
    buckler--or safety, or wisdom, which procures it (compare  Proverbs 3:21 Proverbs 8:14 Proverbs 18:1 Job 6:13 Job 12:13 ). 
 
    layeth up--provides, ever ready.

title: Proverbs 2:8
text:
8. keepeth ... way--God defends the right way, and those in it. 
 
    saints--objects of favor (compare  Psalms 4:3 , &c.). He guides and guards them.

title: Proverbs 2:9
text:
9. Then--emphatic, in such a case. 
 
    righteousness ... path--all parts of duty to God and man.

title: Proverbs 2:10
text: 10, 11. Idea of  Proverbs 2:9 , amplified; on terms, compare  Proverbs 2:2 Proverbs 2:4  2:4|.

title: Proverbs 2:12
text:
12-15. To deliver--as from great danger ( Proverbs 6:5 ). 
 
    way ... man-- ( Psalms 1:1 ). 
 
    froward things--perversity ( Proverbs 6:14 Proverbs 23:23 ), what is opposed to truth.

title: Proverbs 2:13
text:
13. paths of uprightness--or, "plainness." 
 
    walk--habitually act;

title: Proverbs 2:14
text:
14. and that with pleasure, in ignorance of good and pursuit of evil. 
 
    frowardness--Not only their own perversity, but that of others is their delight. They love most the worst things.

title: Proverbs 2:15
text:
15. crooked--tortuous, unprincipled. 
 
    froward--literally, (they) are going back, not only aside from right, but opposite to it.

title: Proverbs 2:16
text:
16-19. Deliverance from another danger. 
 
    the strange woman--This term is often used for harlot, or loose woman ( Judges 11:1 Judges 11:2 ), married ( Proverbs 7:5 Proverbs 7:19 ) or not ( I Kings 11:1 ), so called, because such were, perhaps at first, foreigners, though "strange" may also denote whatever is opposed to right or proper, as "strange fire" ( Numbers 3:4 ); "strange incense" ( Exodus 30:9 ). 
 
    flattereth--literally, "smooths." 
 
    her words-- ( Psalms 5:9 ).

title: Proverbs 2:17
text:
17. guide ... youth--lawful husband ( Jeremiah 3:4 ). 
 
    covenant ... God--of marriage made in God's name.

title: Proverbs 2:18
text:
18. inclineth--sinks down (compare  Numbers 13:31 ). 
 
    the dead--or shades of the departed ( Psalms 88:10 ).

title: Proverbs 2:19
text:
19. that is, such as remain impenitent (compare  Ecclesiastes 7:26 ). 
 
    paths of life-- ( Psalms 16:11 ), opposed to paths unto the dead.

title: Proverbs 2:20
text: 20. That ... way of good--that is, Such is the object of these warnings.

title: Proverbs 2:21
text: 21, 22. (Compare  Psalms 37:3 Psalms 37:9 Psalms 37:22 Psalms 37:27 ).

title: Proverbs 2:22
text:
22. transgressors--or impious rebels (compare  Jeremiah 9:2 ). 
 
    rooted out--utterly destroyed, as trees plucked up by the roots.

title: Proverbs 3:1
text:
Proverbs 3:1-35 . The study of truth commended. God must be feared, honored, and trusted, and filial submission, under chastisement, exhibited. The excellence of wisdom urged and illustrated by its place in the divine counsels. Piety enforced by a contrast of the destiny of the righteous and the wicked. 
 
    1. law [and] commandments--all divine instructions (see on  Psalms 118:29  and  Psalms 119:3 ). 
 
    let thine heart keep--or sincerely observe ( Proverbs 4:13 Proverbs 5:2 ).

title: Proverbs 3:2
text:
2. length ... life--often promised as blessings ( Psalms 21:4 Psalms 91:16 ). 
 
    peace--includes prosperity ( Psalms 125:5 ). 
 
    add--abound to thee.

title: Proverbs 3:3
text:
3. mercy and truth--God's faithfulness to His promises is often expressed by these terms ( Psalms 25:10 Psalms 57:3 ). As attributes of men, they express integrity in a wide sense ( Proverbs 16:6 Proverbs 20:28 ). 
 
    bind ... write ... heart--outwardly adorn and inwardly govern motives.

title: Proverbs 3:4
text:
4. favour--grace, amiability ( Proverbs 22:11 Psalms 45:2 ); united with this, 
 
    a good understanding--(Compare Margin), a discrimination, which secures success. 
 
    in the sight ... man--such as God and man approve.

title: Proverbs 3:5
text: 5. Trust ... heart--This is the center and marrow of true wisdom ( Proverbs 22:19 Proverbs 28:25 ). The positive duty has its corresponding negation in the admonition against self-confidence.

title: Proverbs 3:6
text:
6. ways-- ( Psalms 1:1 ). 
 
    acknowledge--by seeking His wise aid ( Proverbs 16:3 Psalms 37:5 Jeremiah 9:23 Jeremiah 9:24 ). 
 
    direct--literally, "make plain" (compare  Hebrews 12:13 ).

title: Proverbs 3:7
text:
7. (Compare  Proverbs 27:2 Romans 12:16 ). 
 
    fear ... evil--reverentially regarding His law.

title: Proverbs 3:8
text:
8. It--This conduct. 
 
    health--(Compare Margin). 
 
    to thy navel--for all the organs of nourishment. 
 
    marrow--(Compare Margin). 
 
    bones--frame of body. True piety promotes bodily health.

title: Proverbs 3:9
text: 9, 10. (Compare  Proverbs 11:25 Exodus 23:19 Deuteronomy 18:4 Isaiah 32:8 II Corinthians 9:13 ).

title: Proverbs 3:10
text: 10. presses--or wine fats ( Joel 2:24 Joel 3:13 ).

title: Proverbs 3:11
text: 11, 12. The true intent of afflictions considered; they do not contradict the assertion of the blessed state of the pious ( Job 5:17 Hebrews 12:5 Hebrews 12:6 ).

title: Proverbs 3:12
text: 12. he delighteth--or receiveth as denoting reconciliation regarding the offense which produced chastisement.

title: Proverbs 3:13
text:
13. findeth--literally, "reaches," or "obtains by seeking." 
 
    getteth--literally, "draws out," as metals by digging.

title: Proverbs 3:14
text:
14, 15. The figure of  Proverbs 3:13  carried out. 
 
    it--that is, wisdom. 
 
    merchandise of silver--acquisition by trading. 
 
    fine gold--dug gold, solid as a nugget.

title: Proverbs 3:15
text: 15. rubies--gems, or pearls.

title: Proverbs 3:16
text: 16, 17. Wisdom personified as bringing the best blessings (compare  Matthew 6:33 I Timothy 4:8 ).

title: Proverbs 3:17
text: 17. Her ways--such as she directs us to take.

title: Proverbs 3:18
text:
18. Wisdom allegorized as 
 
    a tree of life-- ( Genesis 2:9 Genesis 3:22 ) whose fruit preserves life, gives all that makes living a blessing.

title: Proverbs 3:19
text: 19, 20. The place of wisdom in the economy of creation and providence commends it to men, who, in proportion to their finite powers, may possess this invaluable attribute, and are thus encouraged by the divine example of its use to seek its possession.

title: Proverbs 3:21
text:
21. sound wisdom--(compare  Proverbs 2:7 ). 
 
    let ... eyes--that is, these words of instruction.

title: Proverbs 3:22
text: 22-24. assign reasons in their value for happiness and ornament, guidance and support in dangers, both when waking and sleeping.

title: Proverbs 3:25
text:
25. Be not--or, "You shall not be." 
 
    sudden fear--what causes it ( Proverbs 1:27 ), any unlooked-for evil ( Psalms 46:3 Psalms 91:12 I Peter 3:14 ). 
 
    desolation-- ( Proverbs 1:27 ).

title: Proverbs 3:26
text:
26. The reason; such as are objects of God's favor. 
 
    be thy confidence--literally, "in thy confidence," in the source of thy strength (compare  Nahum 3:9 , for the same construction, Hebrew).

title: Proverbs 3:27
text: 27, 28. Promptly fulfil all obligations both of justice and charity (compare  James 2:15 James 2:16 ).

title: Proverbs 3:29
text: 29, 30. Do not abuse confidence and avoid litigation.

title: Proverbs 3:31
text: 31. oppressor--or man of mischief. The destiny of successful evildoers warns against desiring their lot ( Psalms 37:1 Psalms 37:2 Psalms 37:35 Psalms 37:36 ).

title: Proverbs 3:32
text:
32-35. Reasons for the warning. 
 
    froward-- ( Proverbs 2:15 ). 
 
    secret ... righteous--in their communion ( Amos 3:7 ).

title: Proverbs 3:33
text: 33. curse ... wicked--It abides with them, and will be manifested.

title: Proverbs 3:34
text: 34. The retribution of sinners, as in  Psalms 18:26 .

title: Proverbs 3:35
text:
35. inherit--as a portion. 
 
    shame--or disgrace, as opposed to honor. 
 
    promotion--(Compare Margin); as honor for well-doing makes men conspicuous, so fools are signalized by disgrace.

title: Proverbs 4:1
text:
Proverbs 4:1-27 . To an earnest call for attention to his teachings, the writer adds a commendation of wisdom, preceded and enforced by the counsels of his father and teacher. To this he adds a caution (against the devices of the wicked), and a series of exhortations to docility, integrity, and uprightness. 
 
    1, 2. (Compare  Proverbs 1:8 ). 
 
    to know--in order to know. 
 
    doctrine--the matter of learning ( Proverbs 1:5 ), such as he had received ( Lamentations 3:1 ).

title: Proverbs 4:3
text:
3. father's son--emphatic, a son specially regarded, and so called tender, as an object of special care (compare  I Chronicles 22:7 I Chronicles 29:1 ); an idea further expressed by 
 
    only beloved--or, "as an only son" ( Genesis 22:2 ), though he had brothers (see on  I Chronicles 3:4 ).

title: Proverbs 4:4
text:
4. He taught--or directed me. 
 
    retain--as well as receive. 
 
    keep ... and live--observe, that you may live ( Proverbs 7:2 ).

title: Proverbs 4:5
text:
5. Get--as a possession not to be given up. 
 
    neither decline--that is, from obeying my word.

title: Proverbs 4:6
text: 6. Not only accept but love wisdom, who will keep thee from evil, and evil from thee.

title: Proverbs 4:7
text:
7. (Compare  Job 28:28 ). 
 
    getting--or possession; a desire for wisdom is wise.

title: Proverbs 4:8
text:
8. As you highly esteem her, she will raise you to honor. 
 
    embrace her--with fond affection.

title: Proverbs 4:9
text:
9. ornament--such as the chaplet or wreath of conquerors. 
 
    deliver--(Compare  Genesis 14:20 ). The allusion to a shield, contained in the Hebrew, suggests protection as well as honor (compare  Proverbs 4:6 ).

title: Proverbs 4:10
text: 10. (Compare  Proverbs 2:1 Proverbs 3:2 ).

title: Proverbs 4:11
text:
11, 12. way of wisdom--which it prescribes. 
 
    led thee--literally, "caused thee to tread," as a path ( Psalms 107:7 ). 
 
    not be straitened--have ample room ( Psalms 18:36 ).

title: Proverbs 4:13
text: 13. (Compare  Proverbs 3:18 ). The figure of laying hold with the hand suggests earnest effort.

title: Proverbs 4:14
text: 14. (Compare  Psalms 1:1 ). Avoid all temptations to the beginning of evil.

title: Proverbs 4:16
text: 16, 17. The reason is found in the character of sinners, whose zeal to do evil is forcibly depicted ( Proverbs 6:4 Psalms 36:5 ). They live by flagrant vices ( Proverbs 1:13 ). Some prefer to render, "Their bread is wickedness, their drink violence" (compare  Job 15:16 Job 34:7 ).

title: Proverbs 4:18
text: 18, 19. As shining light increases from twilight to noonday splendor, so the course of the just increases in purity, but that of the wicked is as thickest darkness, in which one knows not on what he stumbles.

title: Proverbs 4:20
text: 20-22. (Compare  Proverbs 4:10 Proverbs 4:13 Proverbs 3:8 , &c.).

title: Proverbs 4:22
text: 22. health ... flesh--by preserving from vices destructive of health.

title: Proverbs 4:23
text: 23. with all diligence--or, "above," or "more than all," custody (compare Margin), all that is kept (compare  Ezekiel 38:7 ), because the heart is the depository of all wisdom and the source of whatever affects life and character ( Matthew 12:35 Matthew 15:19 ).

title: Proverbs 4:24
text:
24. a froward mouth--that is, a mouth, or words of ill nature. The Hebrew word differs from that used ( Proverbs 2:15 Proverbs 3:32 ). 
 
    perverse--or, "quarreling." 
 
    lips--or, "words."

title: Proverbs 4:25
text: 25. Let ... before thee--that is, pursue a sincere and direct purpose, avoiding temptations.

title: Proverbs 4:26
text: 26. Ponder--Consider well; a wise course results from wise forethought.

title: Proverbs 4:27
text: 27. (Compare  Proverbs 4:25 ). Avoid all by-paths of evil ( Deuteronomy 2:27 Deuteronomy 17:11 ). A life of integrity requires attention to heart, speech, eyes, and conduct.

title: Proverbs 5:1
text:
Proverbs 5:1-23 . A warning against the seductive arts of wicked women, enforced by considering the advantages of chastity, and the miserable end of the wicked. 
 
    1. This connection of wisdom and understanding is frequent ( Proverbs 2:2 Proverbs 3:7 ); the first denotes the use of wise means for wise ends; the other, the exercise of a proper discrimination in their discovery.

title: Proverbs 5:2
text:
2. regard--or, "observe." 
 
    keep--preserve constantly.

title: Proverbs 5:3
text: 3. (Compare  Proverbs 2:16 ). Her enticing promises are deceitful.

title: Proverbs 5:4
text: 4. her end--literally, "her future," in sense of reward, what follows (compare  Psalms 37:37 Psalms 73:17 ). Its nature is evinced by the use of figures, opposite those of  Proverbs 5:3 . The physical and moral suffering of the deluded profligate are notoriously terrible.

title: Proverbs 5:5
text: 5. feet ... , steps--that is, course of life ends in death.

title: Proverbs 5:6
text: 6. her ways ... know--Some prefer, "that she may not ponder the path of life," &c.; but perhaps a better sense is, "her ways are varied, so as to prevent your knowledge of her true character, and so of true happiness."

title: Proverbs 5:8
text: 8, 9. Avoid the slightest temptation.

title: Proverbs 5:9
text:
9. thine honour--in whatever consisting, strength ( Proverbs 3:13 ) or wealth. 
 
    thy years--by cutting them off in dissipation. 
 
    unto the cruel--for such the sensual are apt to become.

title: Proverbs 5:10
text:
10. wealth--literally, "strength," or the result of it. 
 
    labours--the fruit of thy painful exertions ( Psalms 127:2 ). There may be a reference to slavery, a commuted punishment for death due the adulterer ( Deuteronomy 22:22 ).

title: Proverbs 5:11
text:
11. at the last--the end, or reward (compare  Proverbs 5:4 ). 
 
    mourn--roar in pain. 
 
    flesh and ... body--the whole person under incurable disease.

title: Proverbs 5:12
text: 12-14. The ruined sinner vainly laments his neglect of warning and his sad fate in being brought to public disgrace.

title: Proverbs 5:14
text: 14. evil--for affliction, as in  Genesis 19:20 Genesis 49:15 .

title: Proverbs 5:15
text: 15-20. By figures, in which well, cistern, and fountain ( Proverbs 5:15 Proverbs 5:18 ) represent the wife, and rivers of waters ( Proverbs 5:16 ) the children, men are exhorted to constancy and satisfaction in lawful conjugal enjoyments. In  Proverbs 5:16 , fountains (in the plural) rather denote the produce or waters of a spring, literally, "what is from a spring," and corresponds with "rivers of waters."

title: Proverbs 5:17
text: 17. only thine own--harlots' children have no known father.

title: Proverbs 5:18
text: 18. wife ... youth--married in youth.

title: Proverbs 5:19
text:
19. loving ... roe--other figures for a wife from the well-known beauty of these animals. 
 
    breasts--(Compare  Song of Solomon 1:13 Ezekiel 23:3 Ezekiel 23:8 ). 
 
    ravished--literally, "intoxicated," that is, fully satisfied.

title: Proverbs 5:21
text: 21. The reason, God's eye is on you,

title: Proverbs 5:22
text: 22, 23. and He will cause sin to bring its punishment.

title: Proverbs 5:23
text:
23. without instruction--literally, "in want of instruction," having refused it (compare  Job 13:18 Hebrews 11:24 ). 
 
    go astray--literally, "be drunken." The word "ravished" ( Proverbs 5:19 ) here denotes fulness of punishment.

title: Proverbs 6:1
text:
Proverbs 6:1-35 . After admonitions against suretyship and sloth (compare  Proverbs 6:6-8 ), the character and fate of the wicked generally are set forth, and the writer ( Proverbs 6:20-35 ) resumes the warnings against incontinence, pointing out its certain and terrible results. This train of thought seems to intimate the kindred of these vices. 
 
    1, 2. if--The condition extends through both verses. 
 
    be surety--art pledged. 
 
    stricken ... hand--bargained (compare  Job 17:3 ). 
 
    with a stranger--that is, for a friend (compare  Proverbs 11:15 Proverbs 17:18 ).

title: Proverbs 6:3
text:
3. come ... friend--in his power. 
 
    humble ... sure thy friend--urge as a suppliant; that is, induce the friend to provide otherwise for his debt, or secure the surety.

title: Proverbs 6:4
text: 4, 5. The danger requires promptness.

title: Proverbs 6:6
text: 6-8. The improvident sluggards usually want sureties. Hence, such are advised to industry by the ant's example.

title: Proverbs 6:9
text: 9, 10. Their conduct graphically described;

title: Proverbs 6:11
text:
11. and the fruits of their self-indulgence and indolence presented. 
 
    as ... travellerh--literally, "one who walks backwards and forwards," that is, a highwayman. 
 
    armed man--that is, one prepared to destroy.

title: Proverbs 6:12
text: 12. A naughty person--literally, "A man of Belial," or of worthlessness, that is, for good, and so depraved, or wicked (compare  I Samuel 25:25 I Samuel 30:22 , &c.). Idleness and vice are allied. Though indolent in acts, he actively and habitually (walketh) is ill-natured in speech ( Proverbs 4:24 ).

title: Proverbs 6:13
text: 13, 14. If, for fear of detection, he does not speak, he uses signs to carry on his intrigues. These signs are still so used in the East.

title: Proverbs 6:14
text:
14. Frowardness--as in  Proverbs 2:14 . 
 
    deviseth--literally, "constructs, as an artisan." 
 
    mischief--evil to others. 
 
    discord--especially litigation. Cunning is the talent of the weak and lazy.

title: Proverbs 6:15
text:
15. Suddenness aggravates evil (compare  Proverbs 6:11 Proverbs 29:1 ). 
 
    calamity--literally, "a crushing weight." 
 
    broken--shivered as a potter's vessel; utterly destroyed ( Psalms 2:9 ).

title: Proverbs 6:16
text: 16-19. six ... seven--a mode of speaking to arrest attention ( Proverbs 30:15 Proverbs 30:18 Job 5:19 ).

title: Proverbs 6:17
text: 17. proud look--literally, "eyes of loftiness" ( Psalms 131:1 ). Eyes, tongue, &c., for persons.

title: Proverbs 8:1
text:
Proverbs 8:1-36 . Contrasted with sensual allurements are the advantages of divine wisdom, which publicly invites men, offers the best principles of life, and the most valuable benefits resulting from receiving her counsels. Her relation to the divine plans and acts is introduced, as in  Proverbs 3:19 Proverbs 3:20 , though more fully, to commend her desirableness for men, and the whole is closed by an assurance that those finding her find God's favor, and those neglecting ruin themselves. Many regard the passage as a description of the Son of God by the title, Wisdom, which the older Jews used (and by which He is called in  Luke 11:49 ), as  John 1:1 , &c., describes Him by that of Logos, the Word. But the passage may be taken as a personification of wisdom: for, (1) Though described as with God, wisdom is not asserted to be God. (2) The use of personal attributes is equally consistent with a personification, as with the description of a real person. (3) The personal pronouns used accord with the gender (feminine) of wisdom constantly, and are never changed to that of the person meant, as sometimes occurs in a corresponding use of spirit, which is neuter in Greek, but to which masculine pronouns are often applied ( John 16:14 ), when the acts of the Holy Spirit are described. (4) Such a personification is agreeable to the style of this book (compare  Proverbs 1:20 Proverbs 3:16 Proverbs 3:17 Proverbs 4:8 Proverbs 6:20-22 Proverbs 9:1-4 ), whereas no prophetical or other allusions to the Saviour or the new dispensation are found among the quotations of this book in the New Testament, and unless this be such, none exist. (5) Nothing is lost as to the importance of this passage, which still remains a most ornate and also solemn and impressive teaching of inspiration on the value of wisdom. 
 
    1-4. The publicity and universality of the call contrast with the secrecy and intrigues of the wicked ( Proverbs 7:8 , &c.).

title: Proverbs 8:13
text:
13. For such is the effect of the fear of God, by which hatred to evil preserves from it.

title: Proverbs 8:14
Proverbs 8:15

text: 18. durable riches ... righteousness--Such are the "riches," enduring sources of happiness in moral possessions (compare  Proverbs 3:16 ).

title: Proverbs 8:19
text: 19. (Compare  Proverbs 8:11 Proverbs 3:16 ).

title: Proverbs 8:22
text:
22-31. Strictly, God's attributes are part of Himself. Yet, to the poetical structure of the whole passage, this commendation of wisdom is entirely consonant. In order of time all His attributes are coincident and eternal as Himself. But to set forth the importance of wisdom as devising the products of benevolence and power, it is here assigned a precedence. As it has such in divine, so should it be desired in human, affairs (compare  Proverbs 3:19 ). 
 
    possessed--or, "created"; in either sense, the idea of precedence. 
 
    in the beginning--or simply, "beginning," in apposition with "me." 
 
    before ... of old--preceding the most ancient deeds.

title: Proverbs 8:23
text: 23. I was set up--ordained, or inaugurated ( Psalms 2:6 ). The other terms carry out the idea of the earliest antiquity, and illustrate it by the details of creation ( Proverbs 8:24-29 ).

title: Proverbs 8:24

24. brought forth--(Compare  Psalms 90:2 ). 
 
    abounding--or, "laden with water."

title: Proverbs 8:26
text:
26. fields--or, "out places," "deserts," as opposite to (habitable) "world." 
 
    highest part--or, "sum," all particles together,

title: Proverbs 8:27
text: 27. when he set ... depth--marked out the circle, according to the popular idea of the earth, as circular, surrounded by depths on which the visible concave heavens rested.

title: Proverbs 8:28
text: 28. established ... deep--that is, so as to sustain the waters above and repress those below the firmament ( Genesis 1:7-11 Job 26:8 ).

text:

title: Proverbs 8:30
text: 30, 31. one brought up--an object of special and pleasing regard. The bestowal of wisdom on men is represented by its finding a delightful residence and pleasing God.

title: Proverbs 8:32
text: 32-36. Such an attribute men are urged to seek.

title: Proverbs 8:34
text: 34. watching ... waiting--literally, "so as to watch"; wait, denoting a most sedulous attention.

title: Proverbs 8:35
text: 35. (Compare  Luke 13:23 Luke 13:24 ).

36. sinneth ... me--or better, "missing me," as opposed to "finding" ( Proverbs 8:35 ).

title: Proverbs 9:1
text:
Proverbs 9:1-18 . The commendation of wisdom is continued, under the figure of a liberal host, and its provisions under that of a feast (compare  Luke 14:16-24 ). The character of those who are invited is followed by a contrasted description of the rejectors of good counsel; and with the invitations of wisdom are contrasted the allurement of the wicked woman. 
 
    1. house--(compare  Proverbs 8:34 ). 
 
    her--or, "its" (the house). 
 
    seven pillars--the number seven for many, or a sufficiency ( Proverbs 6:31 ).

title: Proverbs 9:2
text:
2. mingled--to enhance the flavor ( Proverbs 23:30 Isaiah 5:22 ). 
 
    furnished--literally, "set out," "arranged."

title: Proverbs 9:3
text:
3. maidens--servants to invite (compare  Psalms 68:11 Isaiah 40:9 ).

text: 4-6. (Compare  Proverbs 1:4 Proverbs 6:32 ). Wisdom not only supplies right but forbids wrong principles.

title: Proverbs 9:7
text:
7, 8. shame--(Compare  Proverbs 3:35 ).

title: Proverbs 10:1
text:
Proverbs 10:1-32 . Here begins the second part of the book,  Proverbs 10:1-22:16 , which, with the third,  Proverbs 22:16-25:28 , contains series of proverbs whose sense is complete in one or two verses, and which, having no logical connection, admit of no analysis. The parallelisms of  Proverbs 10:1-15:33  are mostly antithetic; and those of  Proverbs 16:1-22:16 , synthetic. The evidences of art in the structure are very clear, and indicate, probably, a purpose of facilitating the labor of memorizing. 
 
    1. wise [and] foolish--as they follow or reject the precepts of wisdom. 
 
    maketh ... father--or, "gladdens a father." 
 
    heaviness--or, "grief."

title: Proverbs 10:2
text:
2. Treasures ... nothing--that is, Ill-gotten gains give no true happiness (compare  Proverbs 4:17 Matthew 6:19 ). 
 
    righteousness--especially beneficence ( Psalms 112:9 ). 
 
    death--the greatest of all evils.

title: Proverbs 10:3
text: 3. (Compare  Psalms 37:16-20 ). The last clause is better: "He will repel the greedy desires of the wicked."

title: Proverbs 10:4
text:
4. slack--literally, "deceitful," failing of its purpose (compare  Hosea 7:16 ). 
 
    maketh rich--(compare  Proverbs 10:22 ).

title: Proverbs 10:5
text:
5. son--as  Proverbs 1:8 Proverbs 1:10 , and often. 
 
    sleepeth--in indolence, and not for rest.

title: Proverbs 10:6
text: 6. Blessings--literally, "Praises." The last clause is better: "The mouth of the wicked covereth (or concealeth) violence (or mischievous devices)" to be executed in due time ( Psalms 5:9 Psalms 10:7 Romans 3:14 ), and hence has no praises (compare  Proverbs 10:11 ).

title: Proverbs 10:7
text:
7. blessed--literally, "for a blessing," or praise. 
 
    shall rot--literally, "be worm-eaten," useless and disgusting.

title: Proverbs 10:8
text:
8. wise, &c.--(compare  Proverbs 9:8 Proverbs 9:9 Proverbs 9:16 ), opposed to

    fall--headlong, suddenly.

title: Proverbs 10:9
text:
9. perverteth his ways--acts deceitfully. 
 
    known--discovered and punished.

text: 10. Two vices contrasted; hypocrisy, or insinuating evil against one ( Proverbs 6:13 Psalms 35:19 ), and rashness of speech. In each case, the results are on the evildoers.

title: Proverbs 10:11
text: 11. a well--or, "source" of good to himself and others ( John 7:37 John 7:38 ). On last clause, see on  Proverbs 10:5 .

title: Proverbs 10:12
text:
12. strifes--or, "litigations." 
 
    covereth--by forgiveness and forbearance.

title: Proverbs 10:13
text:
13. In the lips ... found--hence, not beaten, as the wicked-speaking fool. 
 
    void of understanding-- ( Proverbs 6:32 Proverbs 7:7 ).

title: Proverbs 10:14
text:
14. lay up knowledge--that is, as treasures for good use. 
 
    mouth ... destruction--or, "as to the mouth," &c., destruction is near; they expose themselves to evil by prating.

title: Proverbs 10:15
text: 15. Both by trusting in "uncertain riches" ( I Timothy 6:17 ), or by the evils of poverty ( Proverbs 30:9 ), men, not fearing God, fall into dangers.

title: Proverbs 10:16
text: 16. The industry of the righteous is alone truly successful, while the earnings of the wicked tempt and lead to sin.

title: Proverbs 10:17
text:
17. keepeth--observes ( Proverbs 3:18 Proverbs 4:22 ). 
 
    refuseth--or, "turns from reproof," which might direct him aright.

title: Proverbs 10:18
text: 18. Both vices must one day be known and punished, and hence their folly.

title: Proverbs 10:19
text: 19. Much speech involves risk of sin; hence the wisdom of restraining the tongue ( Psalms 39:1 James 1:26 ).

title: Proverbs 10:20
text: 20. Right speech is the fruit of a good heart, but the wicked show theirs to be useless.

title: Proverbs 10:21
text: 21. Fools not only fail to benefit others, as do the righteous, but procure their own ruin (compare  Proverbs 10:11 Proverbs 10:17 Hosea 4:6 ).

title: Proverbs 10:22
text: 22. it maketh, &c.--"it" is emphatic. Riches from God are without the sorrow of ill-gotten wealth (compare  Ecclesiastes 2:21-23 I Timothy 6:9 I Timothy 6:10 I Timothy 6:17 ).

title: Proverbs 10:23
text: 23. Sin is the pleasure of the wicked; wisdom that of the good.

title: Proverbs 10:24
text: 24. it--the very thing. The wicked get dreaded evil; the righteous, desired good.

title: Proverbs 10:25
text:
25. (Compare  Psalms 1:4 Psalms 37:9 Psalms 37:10 Psalms 37:36 ). 
 
    righteous ... foundation--well laid and firm ( Matthew 7:24 Matthew 7:25 ).

title: Proverbs 10:26
text: 26. that is, causes vexation.

title: Proverbs 10:27
text: 27. (Compare  Proverbs 9:11 Psalms 55:23 ).

title: Proverbs 10:28
text:
28. gladness--in confidence of realizing it. 
 
    expectation ... perish--in disappointment.

title: Proverbs 10:29
text: 29. The way, &c.--that is, God's providence sustains the righteous and overthrows the wicked ( Hosea 14:9 ).

title: Proverbs 10:30
text:
30. (Compare  Proverbs 12:3 Psalms 37:9-11 Psalms 102:28 ). 
 
    earth--or, "land of promise."

title: Proverbs 10:31
text:
31. bringeth forth--literally, "germinates" as a plant. 
 
    froward--(Compare  Proverbs 2:12 Proverbs 2:14 ). 
 
    cut off--as an unproductive plant.

title: Proverbs 10:32
text:
32. know--regard and provide for ( Psalms 1:6 ). 
 
    frowardness--all kinds of deceit and ill-nature. The word is plural.

title: Proverbs 11:1
text:
Proverbs 11:1-31 . 
 
    1. (Compare Margin). The Hebrews used stones for weights. 
 
    just--complete in measure.

title: Proverbs 11:2
text: 2. Self-conceit is unteachable; the humble grow wise (compare  Proverbs 16:18 Proverbs 18:12 ).

title: Proverbs 11:3
text:
3. guide--to lead, as a shepherd ( Proverbs 6:7 Psalms 78:52 ). 
 
    perverseness--ill-nature. 
 
    destroy--with violence.

title: Proverbs 11:4
text:
4. (Compare  Proverbs 10:2 ). 
 
    wrath--that is, of God.

title: Proverbs 11:5
text: 5. direct--or, "make plain"; wicked ways are not plain ( Proverbs 13:17 ).

title: Proverbs 11:6
text: 6. deliver them--that is, from evil, which the wicked suffer by their own doings ( Proverbs 5:22 Psalms 9:16 ).

title: Proverbs 11:7
text:
7. expectation ... perish--for death cuts short all his plans ( Luke 16:25 ). 
 
    hope of unjust--better, "hope of wealth," or "power" (compare  Isaiah 40:29 , Hebrew). This gives an advance on the sentiment of the first clause. Even hopes of gain die with him.

title: Proverbs 11:8
text: 8. Perhaps the trouble prepared by the wicked, and which he inherits (compare  Proverbs 11:6 ).

title: Proverbs 11:9
text: 9. (Compare  Psalms 35:16 Daniel 11:32 ). The just is saved by superior discernment.

title: Proverbs 11:10
text: 10, 11. The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.

title: Proverbs 11:11
text: 11. By the blessing--implying active benevolence.

title: Proverbs 11:12
text:
12. despiseth--or, "reviles," a course contrasted with the prudent silence of the wise. 
 
    holdeth his peace--as if neither hearing nor telling.

title: Proverbs 11:13
text: 13. tale-bearer--(Compare Margin), one trading as a peddler in scandal, whose propensity to talk leads him to betray confidence.

title: Proverbs 11:14
text:
14. counsel--the art of governing ( Proverbs 1:5 ). 
 
    counsellors--literally, "one giving counsel"; the participle used as a collective.

title: Proverbs 11:15
text:
15. (Compare  Proverbs 6:1 ). 
 
    suretiship--(Compare Margin), the actors put for the action, which may be lawfully hated.

title: Proverbs 11:16
text: 16. retaineth--or literally, "lay hold of as a support." Honor is to a feeble woman thus as valuable as riches to men.

title: Proverbs 11:17
text:
17. merciful--kind to others; opposed to cruel. Such benefit themselves by doing good to others (compare  Proverbs 24:5 ), while the cruel injure themselves as well as others. 
 
    flesh--that is, his body, by penuriousness ( Colossians 2:23 ).

title: Proverbs 11:18
text:
18. a deceitful work--or, "wages," which fail to satisfy, or flee away ( Proverbs 10:2 Proverbs 23:5 ). 
 
    sure reward--or, "gain," as from trading ( Hosea 10:12 Galatians 6:8 Galatians 6:9 ).

title: Proverbs 11:19
text: 19. Inference from  Proverbs 11:18  (compare  Proverbs 11:5 Proverbs 11:6 Proverbs 10:16 ).

title: Proverbs 11:20
text:
20. (Compare  Proverbs 11:5 ). 
 
    froward--as in  Proverbs 2:15 , opposed to the simplicity and purity of the upright. 
 
    in their way--or, "conduct."

title: Proverbs 11:21
text: 21. The combined power of the wicked cannot free them from just punishment, while the unaided children of the righteous find deliverance by reason of their pious relationship ( Psalms 37:25 Psalms 37:26 ).

title: Proverbs 11:22
text: 22. Jewels were often suspended from the nose ( Genesis 24:47 Isaiah 3:21 ). Thus adorned, a hog disgusts less than a fair and indiscreet woman.

title: Proverbs 11:23
text:
23. (Compare  Proverbs 10:28 ). 
 
    wrath--is that of God.

title: Proverbs 11:24
text: 24-31. The scope of the whole is a comment on  Proverbs 11:23 . Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

title: Proverbs 11:25
text:
25. liberal soul--(Compare Margin). 
 
    made fat--prospers ( Proverbs 28:25 Deuteronomy 32:15 Luke 6:38 ). 
 
    watereth ... watered--a common figure for blessing.

title: Proverbs 11:26
text:
26. Another example of the truth of  Proverbs 11:23 ; the miser loses reputation, though he saves corn. 
 
    selleth it--that is at a fair price.

title: Proverbs 11:27
text:
27. good [and] mischief--that is, of others. 
 
    procureth ... seeketh--implying success.

title: Proverbs 11:28
text:
28. (Compare  Proverbs 10:15 Psalms 49:6 I Timothy 6:17 ). 
 
    righteous ... branch-- ( Psalms 1:3 Jeremiah 17:8 ).

title: Proverbs 11:29
text:
29. troubleth--as  Proverbs 15:27  explains, by greediness for gain (compare  Proverbs 11:17 ). 
 
    inherit ... wind--Even successful, his gains are of no real value. So the fool, thus acting, either comes to poverty, or heaps up for others.

title: Proverbs 11:30
text:
30. a tree of life--Blessings to others proceed from the works of the righteous ( Proverbs 3:18 ). 
 
    winneth souls--(Compare Margin) to do them good as opposed to  Proverbs 6:25 Ezekiel 13:18  (compare  Luke 5:10 ).

title: Proverbs 11:31
text: 31. Behold--Thus calling attention to the illustrations (compare  Proverbs 11:23 ), the sentiment of which is confirmed even in time, not excluding future rewards and punishments.

title: Proverbs 12:1
text:
Proverbs 12:1-28 . 
 
    1. loveth knowledge--as the fruit of instruction or training ( Proverbs 1:2 ). 
 
    hateth reproof-- ( Proverbs 10:17 ). 
 
    brutish--stupid, regardless of his own welfare ( Psalms 49:10 Psalms 73:22 ).

title: Proverbs 12:3
text:
3. Wickedness cannot give permanent prosperity. 
 
    root ... not be moved--firm as a flourishing tree-- ( Psalms 1:3 Psalms 15:5 Jeremiah 17:8 ).

title: Proverbs 12:4
text:
4. A virtuous woman--in the wide sense of well-disposed to all moral duties ( Proverbs 31:10 ). 
 
    maketh ashamed--that is, by misconduct. 
 
    rottenness--an incurable evil.

title: Proverbs 12:5
text:
5. thoughts--or, "purposes." 
 
    are right--literally, "are judgment," that is, true decisions. 
 
    counsels--(Compare  Proverbs 11:14 ). 
 
    deceit--contrary to truth and honesty.

title: Proverbs 12:6
text:
6. The words--or, "expressed designs" of the wicked are for evil purposes. 
 
    the mouth--or, "words" of the righteous delivering instead of ensnaring men.

title: Proverbs 12:7
text: 7. Such conduct brings a proper return, by the destruction of the wicked and well-being of the righteous and his family.

title: Proverbs 12:8
text:
8. despised--as opposed to commended ( Proverbs 11:12 ). 
 
    perverse heart--or, "wicked principles," as opposed to one of wisdom.

title: Proverbs 12:9
text:
9. despised--held in little repute, obscure ( I Samuel 18:23 Isaiah 3:5 ). 
 
    hath a servant--implying some means of honest living. 
 
    honoureth himself--is self-conceited.

title: Proverbs 12:10
text:
10. regardeth--literally, "knoweth" ( Psalms 1:6 ). 
 
    mercies ... cruel--as acts of compassion ungraciously rendered to the needy. The righteous more regards a beast than the wicked a man.

title: Proverbs 12:11
text: 11. The idler's fate is the result of indolence and want of principle ( Proverbs 6:32 Proverbs 7:7 ).

title: Proverbs 12:12
text:
12. the wicked ... evil--They love the crafty arts of deception. 
 
    the root ... fruit--their own resources supply them; or, it may be rendered: "He (God) giveth, or, sets ( Ezekiel 17:22 ) the root of the righteous," and hence it is firm: or, the verb is impersonal; "As to the root ... it is firm" ( Proverbs 17:19 ).

title: Proverbs 12:13
text: 13, 14. The wicked is snared, &c.--The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.

title: Proverbs 12:15
text: 15. The way ... eyes--The fool is self-conceited (compare  Proverbs 12:1 Proverbs 1:32 Proverbs 10:17 James 3:17 ).

title: Proverbs 12:16
text: 16. prudent ... shame--He is slow to denounce his insulters ( James 1:19 ).

title: Proverbs 12:18
text:
18. speaketh--literally, "speaketh hastily," or indiscreetly ( Psalms 106:33 ), as an angry man retorts harsh and provoking invectives. 
 
    tongue ... health--by soothing and gentle language.

title: Proverbs 12:19
text: 19. Words of truth are consistent, and stand all tests, while lies are soon discovered and exposed.

title: Proverbs 12:20
text: 20. that imagine--or, "plan" ( Proverbs 3:29 ). They design a deceitful course, to which, with all its evils and dangers to others and themselves, the happiness of peace-makers is opposed (compare  Matthew 5:9 Romans 12:18 ).

title: Proverbs 12:21
text:
21. no evil--(as in  Psalms 91:10 ), under God's wise limitations ( Romans 8:28 ). 
 
    mischief--as penal evil.

title: Proverbs 12:22
text: 22. deal truly--or, "faithfully," that is, according to promises (compare  John 3:21 ).

title: Proverbs 12:23
text:
23. concealeth--by his modesty ( Proverbs 10:14 Proverbs 11:13 ). 
 
    heart ... proclaimeth--as his lips speak his thoughts (compare  Ecclesiastes 10:3 ).

title: Proverbs 12:24
text:
24. slothful--(Compare Margin), so called because he fails to meet his promises. 
 
    under tribute--not denoting legal taxes, but the obligation of dependence.

title: Proverbs 12:25
text: 25. a good word--one of comfort.

title: Proverbs 12:26
text: 26. more excellent--(Compare Margin); or, "more successful," while the wicked fail; or, we may read it: "The righteous guides his friend, but," &c., that is, The ability of the righteous to aid others is contrasted with the ruin to which the way of the wicked leads themselves.

title: Proverbs 12:27
text:
27. (Compare  Proverbs 12:24 ). 
 
    took in hunting--or, "his venison." He does not improve his advantages. 
 
    the substance ... precious--or, "the wealth of a man of honor is being diligent," or "diligence." 
 
    precious--literally, "honor" ( Ecclesiastes 10:1 ).

title: Proverbs 12:28
text: 28. (Compare  Proverbs 8:8 Proverbs 8:20 , &c.). A sentiment often stated; here first affirmatively, then negatively.

title: Proverbs 13:1
text:
Proverbs 13:1-25 . 
 
    1. (Compare  Proverbs 6:1-5 Proverbs 10:1 Proverbs 10:17 ).

title: Proverbs 13:2
text:
2. shall eat--that is, obtain ( Proverbs 12:14 ). 
 
    transgressors--as in  Proverbs 2:22 . 
 
    violence--or, "mischief" to themselves.

title: Proverbs 13:3
text:
3. He ... mouth ... life--because evil speeches may provoke violence from others. 
 
    he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction--On last clause, compare  Proverbs 10:14 .

title: Proverbs 13:4
text: 4. (Compare  Proverbs 12:11 Proverbs 12:27 ).

title: Proverbs 13:5
text: 5. loathsome ... shame--better, causeth shame and reproach (compare  Proverbs 19:26 ), by slander, &c., which the righteous hates.

title: Proverbs 13:6
text: 6. A sentiment of frequent recurrence, that piety benefits and sin injures.

title: Proverbs 13:7
text: 7. In opposite ways men act hypocritically for gain of honor or wealth.

title: Proverbs 13:8
text: 8. Riches save some from punishment, while others suffer because they will not heed the rebuke of sloth, which makes and keeps them poor.

title: Proverbs 13:9
text:
9. light ... lamp--prosperity; the first, the greater, and it 
 
    rejoiceth--burns brightly, or continues, while the other, at best small, soon fails.

title: Proverbs 13:10
text: 10. The obstinacy which attends self-conceit, produces contention, which the well-advised, thus evincing modesty, avoid.

title: Proverbs 13:11
text:
11. by vanity--or, "nothingness," that is, which is vain or useless to the public (as card playing or similar vices). 
 
    gathereth ... labour--(Compare Margin), little by little, laboriously.

title: Proverbs 13:12
text:
12. desire cometh--is realized. 
 
    a tree of life--or, "cause of happiness."

title: Proverbs 13:13
text: 13. the word--that is, of advice, or, instruction (compare  Proverbs 10:27 Proverbs 11:31 ).

title: Proverbs 13:14
text:
14. (Compare  Proverbs 10:11 ). 
 
    fountain--or, "source of life." 
 
    to depart--(compare  Proverbs 1:2-4 ), or, "for departing," &c., and so gives life.

title: Proverbs 13:15
text:
15. Right perception and action secure good will, while evil ways are difficult as a stony road. The wicked left of God find punishment of sin in sinning. 
 
    hard--or, "harsh" (compare Hebrew:  Deuteronomy 21:4 Jeremiah 5:15 ).

title: Proverbs 13:16
text:
16. dealeth--acts with foresight. 
 
    a fool ... folly--for want of caution.

title: Proverbs 13:17
text:
17. A wicked--or, "unfaithful" 
 
    messenger falleth into mischief--or, "by mischief," or "evil," and so his errand fails. Contrasted is the character of the faithful, whose faithfulness benefits others.

title: Proverbs 13:18
text: 18. (Compare  Proverbs 10:17 Proverbs 12:1 ).

title: Proverbs 13:19
text: 19. Self-denial, which fools will not endure, is essential to success.

title: Proverbs 13:20
text: 20. The benefits of good and evil of bad society are contrasted.

title: Proverbs 13:21
text:
21. (Compare  Proverbs 11:31 ). 
 
    good ... repaid--or, "He (God) will repay good."

title: Proverbs 13:22
text: 22. wealth ... just--While good men's estates remain in their families, God so orders that the gains of sinners enure to the just (compare  Proverbs 28:8 Psalms 37:18 Psalms 37:22 Psalms 37:26 , &c.).

title: Proverbs 13:23
text: 23. The laboring poor prosper more than those who injudiciously or wickedly strive, by fraud and violence, to supersede the necessity of lawful labor.

title: Proverbs 13:24
text:
24. spareth--or, "withholds." 
 
    rod--of correction. 
 
    hateth--or, acts as if he hated him (compare  Proverbs 3:12 Proverbs 8:36 ). 
 
    chasteneth ... betimes--or, "diligently seeks for him all useful discipline."

title: Proverbs 13:25
text: 25. The comparative temporal prosperity of the righteous and wicked, rather than contentment and discontent, is noted.

title: Proverbs 14:1
text:
Proverbs 14:1-35 . 
 
    1. Every wise, &c.--literally, "The wisdoms" (compare  Proverbs 9:1 ) "of women," plural, a distributive form of speech. 
 
    buildeth ... house--increases wealth, which the foolish, by mismanagement, lessen.

title: Proverbs 14:2
text: 2. uprightness--is the fruit of fearing God, as falsehood and ill-nature ( Proverbs 2:15 Proverbs 3:32 ) of despising Him and His law.

title: Proverbs 14:3
text: 3. rod of pride--that is, the punishment of pride, which they evince by their words. The words of the wise procure good to them.

title: Proverbs 14:4
text: 4. crib is clean--empty; so "cleanness of teeth" denotes want of food (compare  Amos 4:6 ). Men get the proper fruit of their doings ( Galatians 6:7 ).

title: Proverbs 14:5
text:
5. A faithful witness, &c.--one tested to be such. 
 
    utter lies--or, "breathe out lies"--that is, habitually lies ( Proverbs 6:19 ; compare  Acts 9:1 ). Or the sense is, that habitual truthfulness, or lying, will be evinced in witness-bearing.

title: Proverbs 14:6
text: 6. An humble, teachable spirit succeeds in seeking ( Proverbs 8:9 John 7:17 James 1:5 James 1:6 ).

title: Proverbs 14:7
text: 7. Avoid the society of those who cannot teach you.

title: Proverbs 14:8
text: 8. Appearances deceive the thoughtless, but the prudent discriminate.

title: Proverbs 14:9
text:
9. Fools make a mock at sin--or, "Sin deludes fools." 
 
    righteous ... favour--that is, of God, instead of the punishment of sin.

title: Proverbs 14:10
text: 10. Each one best knows his own sorrows or joys.

title: Proverbs 14:11
text: 11. (Compare  Proverbs 12:7 ). The contrast of the whole is enhanced by that of house and tabernacle, a permanent and a temporary dwelling.

title: Proverbs 14:12
text:
12. end thereof--or, "reward," what results (compare  Proverbs 5:4 ). 
 
    ways of death--leading to it.

title: Proverbs 14:13
text: 13. The preceding sentiment illustrated by the disappointments of a wicked or untimely joy.

title: Proverbs 14:14
text:
14. filled ... ways--receive retribution ( Proverbs 1:31 ). 
 
    a good man ... himself--literally, "is away from such," will not associate with him.

title: Proverbs 14:15
text: 15. The simple ... word--He is credulous, not from love, but heedlessness ( Proverbs 13:16 ).

title: Proverbs 14:16
text:
16. (Compare  Proverbs 3:7 Proverbs 28:14 ). 
 
    rageth--acts proudly and conceitedly.

title: Proverbs 14:17
text:
17. He ... angry--literally, "short of anger" (compare  Proverbs 14:29 , opposite idea). 
 
    man ... hated--that is, the deliberate evildoer is more hated than the rash.

title: Proverbs 14:18
text:
18. inherit--as a portion (compare  Proverbs 3:35 ). 
 
    are crowned--literally, "are surrounded with it," abound in it.

title: Proverbs 14:19
text: 19. Describes the humbling of the wicked by the punishment their sins incur.

title: Proverbs 14:20
text: 20. This sad but true picture of human nature is not given approvingly, but only as a fact.

title: Proverbs 14:21
text: 21. For such contempt of the poor is contrasted as sinful with the virtuous compassion of the good.

title: Proverbs 14:22
text:
22. As usual, the interrogative negative strengthens the affirmative. 
 
    mercy and truth--that is, God's ( Psalms 57:3 Psalms 61:7 ).

title: Proverbs 14:23
text:
23. labour--painful diligence. 
 
    talk ... penury--idle and vain promises and plans.

title: Proverbs 14:24
text:
24. (Compare  Proverbs 3:16 ). 
 
    foolishness ... folly--Folly remains, or produces folly; it has no benefit.

title: Proverbs 14:25
text:
25. Life often depends on truth-telling. 
 
    a deceitful ... lies--He that breathes out lies is deceit, not to be trusted ( Proverbs 14:5 ).

title: Proverbs 14:26
text: 26. The blessings of piety descend to children ( Proverbs 13:22 Proverbs 20:7 Exodus 20:6 ).

title: Proverbs 14:27
text:
27. (Compare  Proverbs 13:14 ). 
 
    fear of the Lord--or, "law of the wise," is wisdom ( Psalms 111:10 ).

title: Proverbs 14:28
text: 28. The teaching of a true political economy.

title: Proverbs 14:29
text:
29. slow ... understanding--(Compare  Proverbs 14:17 ). 
 
    hasty--(Compare  Proverbs 14:17 ). 
 
    exalteth folly--makes it conspicuous, as if delighting to honor it.

title: Proverbs 14:30
