text: 30. A sound heart--both literally and figuratively, a source of health; in the latter sense, opposed to the known effect of evil passions on health.

title: Proverbs 14:31
text: 31. reproacheth his Maker--who is the God of such, as well as of the rich ( Proverbs 22:2 Job 31:15 ; and specially  I Samuel 2:8 Psalms 113:7 ).

title: Proverbs 14:32
text:
32. driven--thrust out violently (compare  Psalms 35:5 Psalms 35:6 ). 
 
    hath hope--trusteth ( Proverbs 10:2 Proverbs 11:4 Psalms 2:12 ), implying assurance of help.

title: Proverbs 14:33
text: 33. resteth--preserved in quietness for use, while fools blazon their folly ( Proverbs 12:23 Proverbs 13:16 ).

title: Proverbs 14:34
text:
34. Righteousness--just principles and actions. 
 
    exalteth--raises to honor. 
 
    is a reproach--brings on them the ill-will of others (compare  Proverbs 13:6 ).

title: Proverbs 14:35
text:
35. wise--discreet or prudent. 
 
    causeth shame-- ( Proverbs 10:5 Proverbs 12:4 ) acts basely.

title: Proverbs 15:1
text:
Proverbs 15:1-33 . 
 
    1. soft--tender or gentle. 
 
    turneth ... wrath--from any one. 
 
    stir up--as a smouldering fire is excited.

title: Proverbs 15:2
text:
2. useth ... aright--commends knowledge by its proper use. 
 
    poureth out--utters abundantly ( Proverbs 12:23 ), and so disgusts others.

title: Proverbs 15:3
text: 3. beholding--watching (compare  Proverbs 5:21 Psalms 66:7 ).

title: Proverbs 15:4
text:
4. A wholesome tongue--(Compare Margin), pacifying and soothing language. 
 
    tree of life-- ( Proverbs 3:18 Proverbs 11:30 ). 
 
    perverseness therein--cross, ill-natured language. 
 
    breach ... spirit--(compare  Isaiah 65:14 , Hebrew), grieves, instead of appeasing.

title: Proverbs 15:5
text:
5. (Compare  Proverbs 4:1 Proverbs 10:17 Proverbs 13:1-18 ). 
 
    is prudent--acts discreetly.

title: Proverbs 15:6
text:
6. treasure--implying utility. 
 
    trouble--vexation and affliction.

title: Proverbs 15:7
text:
7. (Compare  Proverbs 10:20 Proverbs 10:21 ). 
 
    heart ... not so--not right, or vain.

title: Proverbs 15:8
text:
8, 9. The sacrifice [and] prayer--are acts of worship. 
 
    way ... followeth ... righteousness--denote conduct. God's regard for the worship and deeds of the righteous and wicked respectively, so stated in  Psalms 50:17 Isaiah 1:11 .

title: Proverbs 15:10
text:
10. (Compare  Proverbs 10:17 ). 
 
    the way--that in which God would have him to go ( Proverbs 2:13 Psalms 119:1 ).

title: Proverbs 15:11
text:
11. Hell-- ( Psalms 16:10 ). 
 
    destruction--or, "Abaddon," the place of the destroyer. All the unseen world is open to God, much more men's hearts.

title: Proverbs 15:12
text:
12. (Compare  Proverbs 9:8 ). 
 
    go unto the wise--to be instructed.

title: Proverbs 15:13
text:
13. maketh ... countenance--or, "benefits the countenance." 
 
    spirit is broken--and so the countenance is sad.

title: Proverbs 15:14
text: 14. (Compare  Proverbs 10:21 Proverbs 10:22 ). The wise grow wiser, the fools more foolish ( Proverbs 9:9 ).

title: Proverbs 15:15
text:
15. The state of the heart governs the outward condition. 
 
    evil--sad, contrasted with the cheerfulness of a feast.

title: Proverbs 15:16
text: 16. trouble--agitation, implying the anxieties and perplexities attending wealth held by worldlings ( Proverbs 16:18 I Timothy 6:6 ).

title: Proverbs 15:17
text:
17. dinner--or, "allowance" ( II Kings 25:30 ) -- 
 
    of herbs--and that the plainest. 
 
    and hatred--(compare  Proverbs 10:12 Proverbs 10:18 ).

title: Proverbs 15:18
text: 18. (Compare  Proverbs 14:29 Proverbs 16:32 ).

title: Proverbs 15:19
text:
19. The difficulties of the slothful result from want of energy; the righteous find a 
 
    plain [and open] way--literally, "a highway," by diligence ( I Samuel 10:7 Psalms 1:3 ).

title: Proverbs 15:20
text: 20. (Compare  Proverbs 10:1 ).

title: Proverbs 15:21
text: 21. walketh uprightly--and so finds his joy ( Proverbs 3:6 Proverbs 10:23 ).

title: Proverbs 15:22
text: 22. Without counsel--or, "deliberation," implying a wise deference to the opinions of the wise and good, contrasted with rashness.

title: Proverbs 15:23
text: 23. Good advice blesses the giver and receiver.

title: Proverbs 15:24
text: 24. (Compare  Colossians 3:2 ). Holy purposes prevent sinning, and so its evils.

title: Proverbs 15:25
text:
25. The most desolate who have God's aid have more permanent good than the self-reliant sinner ( Proverbs 2:22 Proverbs 12:7 ). 
 
    border--or, "boundary for possessions" ( Psalms 78:54 ).

title: Proverbs 15:26
text: 26. are pleasant words--that is, pleasing to God ( Proverbs 8:8 Proverbs 8:9 ).

title: Proverbs 15:27
text:
27. (Compare  Proverbs 11:17 ). Avarice brings trouble to him and his. 
 
    hateth gifts--or, "bribes" ( Exodus 23:8 Psalms 15:5 ), and is not avaricious.

title: Proverbs 15:28
text: 28. (Compare  Proverbs 15:14 Proverbs 10:11 ). Caution is the fruit of wisdom; rashness of folly.

title: Proverbs 15:29
text: 29. far ... wicked--in His love and favor ( Psalms 22:11 Psalms 119:155 ).

title: Proverbs 15:30
text:
30. light of the eyes-- ( Proverbs 13:9 ). What gives light rejoiceth the heart, by relieving from anxiety as to our course; so 
 
    good report--or, "doctrine" ( Isaiah 28:9 Isaiah 53:1 ), 
 
    maketh ... fat--or, "gives prosperity" ( Proverbs 3:13-17 Proverbs 9:11 ). The last clause is illustrated by the first.

title: Proverbs 15:31
text:
31, 32. (Compare  Proverbs 10:17 ). 
 
    reproof of life--which leads to life. 
 
    abideth ... wise--is numbered among them.

title: Proverbs 15:32
text:
32. refuseth--or, "neglects," "passes by" ( Proverbs 1:25 Proverbs 4:15 ). 
 
    despiseth ... soul--so acts as if esteeming its interests of no value.

title: Proverbs 15:33
text:
33. The fear ... wisdom--Wisdom instructs in true piety. 
 
    before ... humility--(compare  Luke 24:26 I Peter 1:11 ); opposite (compare  Proverbs 16:18 ).

title: Proverbs 16:1
text:
Proverbs 16:1-33 . 
 
    1. preparations--schemes. 
 
    in man--or literally, "to man," belonging, or pertaining to him. 
 
    the answer ... Lord--The efficient ordering is from God: "Man proposes; God disposes."

title: Proverbs 16:2
text:
2. clean--or, "faultless." 
 
    weigheth--or, "tries," "judges," implying that they are faulty ( Proverbs 21:2 Proverbs 24:12 ).

title: Proverbs 16:3
text: 3. (Compare Margin). Rely on God for success to your lawful purposes.

title: Proverbs 16:4
text: 4. for himself--"for its answer," or "purpose," that is, according to God's plan; the wicked are for the day of evil ( Psalms 49:5 Jeremiah 17:18 ); sinning and suffering answer to each other, are indissolubly united.

title: Proverbs 16:5
text: 5. (Compare  Proverbs 3:32 ).

title: Proverbs 16:6
text:
6. By mercy and truth--that is, God's ( Psalms 85:10 ); He effects the atonement, or covering of sin; and the principles of true piety incline men to depart from evil; or, "mercy" and "truth" may be man's, indicative of the gracious tempers which work instrumentally in procuring pardon. 
 
    purged--expiated (as in  Leviticus 16:33 Isaiah 27:9 , Hebrew).

title: Proverbs 16:7
text: 7. Persecutions, of course, excepted.

title: Proverbs 16:8
text: 8. (Compare  Proverbs 15:6 Proverbs 15:16 Proverbs 15:17 ).

title: Proverbs 16:9
text:
9. (Compare  Proverbs 16:3 ). 
 
    directeth--establisheth.

title: Proverbs 16:10
text: 10. The last clause depends on the first, expressing the importance of equity in decisions, so authoritative.

title: Proverbs 16:11
text: 11. are the Lord's ... his work--that is, what He has ordered, and hence should be observed by men.

title: Proverbs 16:12
text: 12. Rulers are rightly expected, by their position, to hate evil; for their power is sustained by righteousness.

title: Proverbs 16:13
text: 13. A specification of the general sentiment of  Proverbs 16:12 .

title: Proverbs 16:14
text: 14. This wrath, so terrible and certain, like messengers of death ( I Kings 2:25 ), can be appeased by the wise.

title: Proverbs 16:15
text:
15. light of ... countenance--favor ( Psalms 4:6 ). 
 
    life--preserves it, or gives blessings which make it valuable. 
 
    the latter rain--fell just before harvest and matured the crop; hence specially valuable ( Deuteronomy 11:14 ).

title: Proverbs 16:16
text: 16. (Compare  Proverbs 3:16 Proverbs 4:5 ).

title: Proverbs 16:17
text:
17. The highway--A common, plain road represents the habitual course of the righteous in departing from evil. 
 
    keepeth--observes.

title: Proverbs 16:18
text:
18, 19. (Compare  Proverbs 15:33 ). Haughtiness and pride imply self-confidence which produces carelessness, and hence 
 
    a fall--literally, "sliding."

title: Proverbs 16:19
text: 19. divide the spoil--that is, conquer. Avoid the society of the proud ( James 4:6 ).

title: Proverbs 16:20
text:
20. handleth a matter--wisely considers "the word," that is, of God (compare  Proverbs 13:13 ). 
 
    trusteth--(Compare  Psalms 2:12 Psalms 118:8 Psalms 118:9 ).

title: Proverbs 16:21
text:
21. wise in heart--who rightly consider duty. 
 
    sweetness of the lips--eloquent discourse, persuades and instructs others.

title: Proverbs 16:22
text: 22. Understanding--or, "discretion," is a constant source of blessing ( Proverbs 13:14 ), benefiting others; but fools' best efforts are folly.

title: Proverbs 16:23
text: 23. The heart is the source of wisdom flowing from the mouth.

title: Proverbs 16:24
text: 24. (Compare  Proverbs 15:26 ). Gentle, kind words, by soothing the mind, give the body health.

title: Proverbs 16:25
text: 25. (Compare  Proverbs 14:2 ).

title: Proverbs 16:26
text: 26. Diligence is a duty due to one's self, for his wants require labor.

title: Proverbs 16:27
text:
27. ungodly man--(Compare  Proverbs 6:12 ). 
 
    diggeth up evil--labors for it. 
 
    in his lips ... fire--His words are calumniating ( James 3:6 ).

title: Proverbs 16:28
text:
28. (Compare  Proverbs 6:14 Proverbs 10:31 ). 
 
    whisperer--prater, talebearer ( Proverbs 18:8 Proverbs 26:20 ).

title: Proverbs 16:29
text:
29. violent man--or, "man of mischief" ( Proverbs 3:31 ). 
 
    enticeth-- ( Proverbs 1:10 ).

title: Proverbs 16:30
text:
30. He shutteth his eyes--denoting deep thought ( Psalms 64:6 ). 
 
    moving his lips--or, "biting his lips"--a determined purpose ( Proverbs 6:13 ).

title: Proverbs 16:31
text:
31. (Compare  Proverbs 20:29 ). 
 
    if--or, which may be supplied properly, or without it the sense is as in  Proverbs 3:16 Proverbs 4:10 , that piety is blessed with long life.

title: Proverbs 16:32
text:
32. (Compare  Proverbs 14:29 ). 
 
    taketh a city--that is, by fighting.

title: Proverbs 16:33
text: 33. Seemingly the most fortuitous events are ordered by God.

title: Proverbs 17:1
text:
Proverbs 17:1-28 . 
 
    1. sacrifices--or, "feasts" made with part of them (compare  Proverbs 7:14 Leviticus 2:3 Leviticus 7:31 ). 
 
    with--literally, "of." 
 
    strife--its product, or attendant.

title: Proverbs 17:2
text:
2. (Compare  Proverbs 14:35 ). 
 
    causeth shame-- ( Proverbs 10:5 ). 
 
    shall ... inheritance--that is, share a brother's part (compare  Numbers 27:4 Numbers 27:7 ).

title: Proverbs 17:3
text: 3. God only knows, as He tries ( Psalms 12:6 Psalms 66:10 ) the heart.

title: Proverbs 17:4
text: 4. Wicked doers and speakers alike delight in calumny.

title: Proverbs 17:5
text:
5. (Compare  Proverbs 14:31 ). 
 
    glad at calamities--rejoicing in others' evil. Such are rightly punished by God, who knows their hearts.

title: Proverbs 17:6
text: 6. Prolonged posterity is a blessing, its cutting off a curse ( Proverbs 13:22 Psalms 109:13-15 ), hence children may glory in virtuous ancestry.

title: Proverbs 17:7
text: 7. Excellent speech--(Compare Margin). Such language as ill suits a fool, as lying (ought to suit) a prince ( Proverbs 16:12 Proverbs 16:13 ).

title: Proverbs 17:8
text: 8. One so corrupt as to take a bribe evinces his high estimate of it by subjection to its influence ( Proverbs 18:16 Proverbs 19:6 ).

title: Proverbs 17:9
text: 9. seeketh love--(Compare Margin). The contrast is between the peace-maker and tale-bearer.

title: Proverbs 17:10
text: 10. Reproof more affects the wise than severe scourging, fools.

title: Proverbs 17:11
text:
11. Such meet just retribution ( I Kings 2:25 ). 
 
    a cruel messenger--one to inflict it.

title: Proverbs 17:12
text: 12. They are less rational in anger than wild beasts.

title: Proverbs 17:13
text:
13. (Compare  Psalms 7:4 Psalms 35:12 ). 
 
    evil--injury to another ( Proverbs 13:21 ).

title: Proverbs 17:14
text:
14. letteth ... water--as a breach in a dam. 
 
    before ... meddled with--before strife has become sharp, or, by an explanation better suiting the figure, before it rolls on, or increases.

title: Proverbs 17:15
text: 15. abomination ... Lord--as reversing His method of acting ( Proverbs 3:32 Proverbs 12:2 ).

title: Proverbs 17:16
text: 16. Though wealth cannot buy wisdom for those who do not love it, yet wisdom procures wealth ( Proverbs 3:16 Proverbs 14:24 ).

title: Proverbs 17:17
text: 17. To the second of these parallel clauses, there is an accession of meaning, that is, that a brother's love is specially seen in adversity.

title: Proverbs 17:18
text:
18. (Compare  Proverbs 6:1-5 Proverbs 11:15 ). 
 
    in the presence, &c.--that is, he either fails to consult his friend, or to follow his advice.

title: Proverbs 17:19
text:
19. strife--contention is, and leads to, sin. 
 
    he that exalteth his gate--gratifies a vain love of costly building. 
 
    seeketh--or, "findeth," as if he sought (compare "loveth death,"  Proverbs 8:36 ).

title: Proverbs 17:20
text: 20. The second clause advances on the first. The ill-natured fail of good, and the cavilling and fault-finding incur evil.

title: Proverbs 17:21
text: 21. (Compare  Proverbs 23:24 ). Different words are rendered by "fool," both denoting stupidity and impiety.

title: Proverbs 17:22
text:
22. (Compare  Proverbs 14:30 Proverbs 15:13 ). The effect of the mind on the body is well known. 
 
    medicine--or, "body," which better corresponds with "bone." 
 
    drieth--as if the marrow were exhausted.

title: Proverbs 17:23
text:
23. a gift ... bosom--Money and other valuables were borne in a fold of the garment, called the bosom. 
 
    to pervert--that is, by bribery.

title: Proverbs 17:24
text: 24. Wisdom ... him--ever an object of regard, while a fool's affections are unsettled.

title: Proverbs 17:25
text: 25. a grief--or cross, vexation (compare  Proverbs 17:21 Proverbs 10:1 ).

title: Proverbs 17:26
text: 26. Also--that is, Equally to be avoided are other sins: punishing good subjects, or resisting good rulers.

title: Proverbs 17:27
text: 27, 28. Prudence of speech is commended as is an excellent or calm spirit, not excited to vain conversation.

title: Proverbs 18:1
text:
Proverbs 18:1-24 . 
 
    1. Through desire ... seeketh--that is, seeks selfish gratification. 
 
    intermeddleth ... wisdom--or, "rushes on" ( Proverbs 17:14 ) against all wisdom, or what is valuable ( Proverbs 2:7 ).

title: Proverbs 18:2
text: 2. that his heart ... itself--that is, takes pleasure in revealing his folly ( Proverbs 12:23 Proverbs 15:2 ).

title: Proverbs 18:3
text:
3. So surely are sin and punishment connected ( Proverbs 16:4 ). 
 
    wicked, for "wickedness," answers to 
 
    ignominy, or the state of such; and 
 
    contempt, the feeling of others to them; and to 
 
    reproach, a manifestation of contempt.

title: Proverbs 18:4
text: 4. Wise speech is like an exhaustless stream of benefit.

title: Proverbs 18:5
text: 5. accept the person--(Compare  Psalms 82:2 ). "It is not good" is to be supplied before "to overthrow."

title: Proverbs 18:6
text: 6, 7. The quarrelsome bring trouble on themselves. Their rash language ensnares them ( Proverbs 6:2 ).

title: Proverbs 18:8
text:
8. (Compare  Proverbs 16:28 ). 
 
    as wounds--not sustained by the Hebrew; better, as "sweet morsels," which men gladly swallow. 
 
    innermost ... belly--the mind, or heart (compare  Proverbs 20:27-30 Psalms 22:14 ).

title: Proverbs 18:9
text:
9. One by failing to get, the other by wasting wealth, grows poor. 
 
    waster--literally, "master of washing," a prodigal.

title: Proverbs 18:10
text:
10. name of the Lord--manifested perfections ( Psalms 8:1 Psalms 20:2 ), as faithfulness, power, mercy, &c., on which men rely. 
 
    is safe--literally, "set on high, out of danger" ( Psalms 18:2 Psalms 91:4 ).

title: Proverbs 18:11
text: 11. contrasts with  Proverbs 18:10  (compare  Proverbs 10:15 ). Such is a vain trust (compare  Psalms 73:6 ).

title: Proverbs 18:12
text: 12. (Compare  Proverbs 15:33 Proverbs 16:18 ).

title: Proverbs 18:13
text: 13. Hasty speech evinces self-conceit, and ensures shame ( Proverbs 26:12 ).

title: Proverbs 18:14
text: 14. infirmity--bodily sickness, or outward evil. The spirit, which sustains, being wounded, no support is left, except, as implied, in God.

title: Proverbs 18:15
text: 15. (Compare  Proverbs 1:5 Proverbs 1:15 Proverbs 1:31 ).

title: Proverbs 18:16
text: 16. (Compare  Proverbs 17:8 Proverbs 17:23 ). Disapproval of the fact stated is implied.

title: Proverbs 18:17
text:
17. One-sided statements are not reliable. 
 
    searcheth--thoroughly ( Proverbs 17:9 Proverbs 17:19 ).

title: Proverbs 18:18
text: 18. The lot--whose disposal is of God ( Proverbs 16:13 ), may, properly used, be a right mode of settling disputes.

title: Proverbs 18:19
text: 19. No feuds so difficult of adjustment as those of relatives; hence great care should be used to avoid them.

title: Proverbs 18:20
text:
20. (Compare  Proverbs 12:14 Proverbs 13:2 ). Men's words are the fruit, or, increase of his lips, and when good, benefit them. 
 
    satisfied with--(Compare  Proverbs 1:31 Proverbs 14:14 ).

title: Proverbs 18:21
text:
21. Death and life--or, the greatest evil and good. 
 
    that love it--that is, the tongue, or its use for good or evil. 
 
    eat ... fruit--(Compare  Proverbs 18:19 James 1:19 ).

title: Proverbs 18:22
text: 22. The old versions supply "good" before the "wife," as the last clause and  Proverbs 19:14  imply (compare  Proverbs 31:10 ).

title: Proverbs 18:23
text: 23. the rich ... roughly--He is tolerated because rich, implying that the estimate of men by wealth is wrong.

title: Proverbs 18:24
text: 24. A man ... friendly--better, "A man ... (is) to, or, may triumph ( Psalms 108:9 ), or, shout for joy ( Psalms 5:11 ), that is, may congratulate himself." Indeed, there is a Friend who is better than a brother; such is the "Friend of sinners" [ Matthew 11:19 Luke 7:34 ], who may have been before the writer's mind.

title: Proverbs 19:1
text:
Proverbs 19:1-29 . 
 
    1. (Compare  Proverbs 28:6 ). "Rich" for fool here. Integrity is better than riches ( Proverbs 15:16 Proverbs 15:17 Proverbs 16:8 ).

title: Proverbs 19:2
text: 2. The last illustrates the first clause. Rashness, the result of ignorance, brings trouble.

title: Proverbs 19:3
text: 3. perverteth ... way--turns him back from right ( Proverbs 13:6 James 1:13 ); and he blames God for his failures.

title: Proverbs 19:4
text: 4. (Compare  Proverbs 14:20 ). Such facts are often adduced with implied disapprobation.

title: Proverbs 19:5
text: 5. Compare  Proverbs 19:9 , where perish explains not escape here (compare  Psalms 88:9 Psalms 88:10 ).

title: Proverbs 19:8
text:
8. (Compare Margin;  Proverbs 15:32 ). 
 
    loveth ... soul--or, "himself," which he evinces by regarding his best interests. 
 
    keepeth--or, "regards."

title: Proverbs 19:10
text: 10. (Compare  Proverbs 17:7 ). The fool is incapable of properly using pleasure as knowledge, yet for him to have it is less incongruous than the undue elevation of servants. Let each abide in his calling ( I Corinthians 7:20 ).

title: Proverbs 19:11
text: 11. (Compare  Proverbs 14:29 Proverbs 16:32 ). This inculcation of a forgiving spirit shows that true religion is always the same ( Matthew 5:22-24 ).

title: Proverbs 19:12
text: 12. (Compare  Proverbs 16:14 Proverbs 16:15 Proverbs 20:2 ). A motive to submission to lawful authority.

title: Proverbs 19:13
text:
13. calamity--literally, "calamities," varied and many. 
 
    continual dropping--a perpetual annoyance, wearing out patience.

title: Proverbs 19:14
text:
14. A contrast of men's gifts and God's, who, though author of both blessings, confers the latter by His more special providence. 
 
    and--or, "but," implying that the evils of  Proverbs 19:13  are only avoided by His care.

title: Proverbs 19:15
text:
15. a deep sleep--a state of utter indifference. 
 
    idle soul--or, "person" (compare  Proverbs 10:4 Proverbs 12:24 ).

title: Proverbs 19:16
text:
16. (Compare  Proverbs 10:17 Proverbs 13:13 ). 
 
    despiseth ... ways--opposed to keeping or observing, neglects ( Proverbs 16:17 ) (as unworthy of regard) his moral conduct.

title: Proverbs 19:17
text:
17. (Compare  Proverbs 14:21 Psalms 37:26 ). 
 
    hath pity--shown by acts (compare Margin).

title: Proverbs 19:18
text:
18. (Compare  Proverbs 13:24 Proverbs 23:13 ). 
 
    let not ... spare--literally, "do not lift up thy soul" ( Psalms 24:4 Psalms 25:1 ), that is, do not desire to his death; a caution to passionate parents against angry chastisement.

title: Proverbs 19:19
text: 19. Repeated efforts of kindness are lost on ill-natured persons.

title: Proverbs 19:20
text:
20. (Compare  Proverbs 13:18-20 ). 
 
    latter end-- ( Proverbs 5:11 ). In youth prepare for age.

title: Proverbs 19:21
text: 21. (Compare  Proverbs 16:1 Proverbs 16:9 Psalms 33:10 Psalms 33:11 ). The failure of man's devices is implied.

title: Proverbs 19:22
text: 22. desire--that is, to do good, indicates a kind disposition ( Proverbs 11:23 ); and the poor thus affected are better than liars, who say and do not.

title: Proverbs 19:23
text:
23. The fear ... life--(Compare  Proverbs 3:2 ). 
 
    abide--or, "remain contented" ( I Timothy 4:8 ). 
 
    not visited with evil-- ( Proverbs 10:3 Psalms 37:25 ), as a judgment, in which sense visit is often used ( Psalms 89:32 Jeremiah 6:15 ).

title: Proverbs 19:24
text: 24. bosom--literally, a wide dish in which the hand was plunged in eating ( Matthew 26:23 ). Compare  Proverbs 26:15 , the sentiment expressed with equal irony and less exaggeration.

title: Proverbs 19:25
text: 25. Such is the benefit of reproof; even the simple profit, much more the wise.

title: Proverbs 19:26
text: 26. Unfilial conduct often condemned ( Proverbs 17:21-25 Proverbs 20:20 Deuteronomy 21:18 Deuteronomy 21:21 ).

title: Proverbs 19:27
text: 27. Avoid whatever leads from truth.

title: Proverbs 19:28
text:
28. ungodly witness--(Compare Margin), one false by bad principles (compare  Proverbs 6:12 ). 
 
    scorneth judgment--sets at naught the dictates of justice. 
 
    devoureth--literally, "swalloweth," as something delightful.

title: Proverbs 19:29
text: 29. Their punishment is sure, fixed, and ready (compare  Proverbs 3:34 Proverbs 10:13 ).

title: Proverbs 20:1
text:
Proverbs 20:1-30 . 
 
    1. mocker--scorner. Such men are made by wine. 
 
    strong drink--made by spicing wine (compare  Isaiah 5:11 Isaiah 5:22 ); and it may include wine. 
 
    raging--or boisterous as a drunkard. 
 
    deceived--literally, "erring," or reeling.

title: Proverbs 20:2
text: 2. (Compare  Proverbs 19:12 ). Men who resist authority injure themselves ( Romans 13:2 ).

title: Proverbs 20:3
text:
3. to cease from strife--or, better, "to dwell from or without strife," denoting the habit of life. 
 
    fool ... meddling-- ( Proverbs 17:14 ).

title: Proverbs 20:4
text: 4. shall ... beg--literally, "ask" (in this sense,  Psalms 109:10 ).

title: Proverbs 20:5
text: 5. Counsel ... water--that is, deeply hidden ( Proverbs 18:4 Psalms 13:2 ). The wise can discern well.

title: Proverbs 20:6
text:
6. Boasters are unreliable. 
 
    goodness--or, "kind disposition."

title: Proverbs 20:7
text: 7. The conduct of good men proclaims their sound principles. God's covenant and their good example secure blessing to their children ( Proverbs 4:26 Psalms 112:1 Psalms 112:2 ).

title: Proverbs 20:8
text: 8. As in  Proverbs 14:35 Proverbs 16:10 Proverbs 16:15 , this is the character of a good king, not of all kings.

title: Proverbs 20:9
text: 9. The interrogation in the affirmative strengthens the implied negation (compare  Job 15:14 Ecclesiastes 7:20 ).

title: Proverbs 20:10
text: 10. Various measures, implying that some are wrong (compare  Proverbs 11:1 Proverbs 16:11 ).

title: Proverbs 20:11
text: 11. The conduct of children even is the best test of principle (compare  Matthew 7:16 ).

title: Proverbs 20:12
text: 12. Hence, of course, God will know all you do ( Psalms 94:9 ).

title: Proverbs 20:13
text:
13. Activity and diligence contrasted with sloth ( Proverbs 6:9 Proverbs 10:11 ). 
 
    lest ... poverty--literally, "be deprived of inheritance."

title: Proverbs 20:14
text: 14. when ... his way--implying that he goes about boasting of his bargains.

title: Proverbs 20:15
text: 15. The contrast denotes the greater value of knowledge (compare  Proverbs 3:14-16 ).

title: Proverbs 20:16
text:
16. Take his garment--implies severe exaction, justified by the surety's rashness. 
 
    a strange woman--by some readings "strangers," but the former here, and in  Proverbs 27:13 , is allowable, and strengthens the sense. The debauchee is less reliable than the merely careless.

title: Proverbs 20:17
text:
17. Bread ... sweet--either as unlawfully ( Proverbs 9:17 ) or easily obtained. 
 
    mouth ... gravel--well expresses the pain and grief given at last.

title: Proverbs 20:18
text: 18. (Compare  Proverbs 15:22 ). Be careful and considerate in important plans.

title: Proverbs 20:19
text:
19. Those who love to tell news will hardly keep secrets. 
 
    flattereth ... lips--(compare Margin;  Proverbs 1:10 ). 
 
    meddle ... him--literally, "join," or "associate with."

title: Proverbs 20:20
text: 20. his lamp--(Compare  Proverbs 13:9 Proverbs 24:20 ).

title: Proverbs 20:21
text: 21. gotten hastily--contrary to God's providence ( Proverbs 28:20 ), implying its unjust or easy attainment; hence the man is punished, or spends freely what he got easily (compare  Proverbs 20:17 ).

title: Proverbs 20:22
text: 22. (Compare  Psalms 27:14 Romans 12:17-19 ).

title: Proverbs 20:23
text: 23. (Compare  Proverbs 20:10 Proverbs 11:1 ).

title: Proverbs 20:24
text:
24. Man's goings--literally, "Stately steppings of a strong man." 
 
    a man--any common man. 
 
    understand--or, "perceive."

title: Proverbs 20:25
text: 25. devoureth ... holy--or, better, "who rashly speaks promises," or "devotes what is holy," consecrating any thing. This suits better the last clause, which expresses a similar view of the results of rashly vowing.

title: Proverbs 20:26
text:
26. (Compare  Proverbs 20:8 ). 
 
    bringeth ... over them--The wheel was used for threshing grain. The figure denotes severity (compare  Amos 1:3 ).

title: Proverbs 20:27
text: 27. The spirit ... Lord--Men's minds are God's gifts, and thus able to search one another (compare  Proverbs 20:5 Proverbs 18:8 Proverbs 18:17 I Corinthians 2:11 ).

title: Proverbs 20:28
text: 28. (Compare  Proverbs 3:3 Proverbs 16:6 Proverbs 16:12 ).

title: Proverbs 20:29
text: 29. The glory of young men ... the beauty of old men--Each age has its peculiar excellence ( Proverbs 16:31 ).

title: Proverbs 20:30
text:
30. blueness--literally, "joining," the process of uniting the edges of a wound throws off purulent matter. 
 
    stripes ... belly--So punishment provides healing of soul ( Proverbs 18:8 ), by deterring from evil courses.

title: Proverbs 21:1
text:
Proverbs 21:1-31 . 
 
    1. rivers--irrigating channels ( Psalms 1:3 ), whose course was easily turned (compare  Deuteronomy 11:10 ). God disposes even kings as He pleases ( Proverbs 16:9 Psalms 33:15 ).

title: Proverbs 21:2
text: 2. (Compare  Proverbs 14:2 Proverbs 16:2-25 ).

title: Proverbs 21:3
text: 3. (Compare  Psalms 50:7-15 Isaiah 1:11 Isaiah 1:17 ).

title: Proverbs 21:4
text:
4. high look--(Compare Margin;  Psalms 131:1 ). 
 
    proud heart--or, "heart of breadth," one that is swollen (compare  Psalms 101:5 ). 
 
    ploughing--better "lamp," a frequent figure for prosperity ( Proverbs 20:20 ); hence joy or delight.

title: Proverbs 21:5
text: 5. The contrast is between steady industry and rashness (compare  Proverbs 19:2 ).

title: Proverbs 21:6
text:
6. The getting--or, "what is obtained" (compare  Job 7:2 Jeremiah 22:13 , Hebrew). 
 
    vanity ... to and fro--as fleeting as chaff or stubble in the wind (compare  Proverbs 20:17-21 Psalms 62:10 ). Such gettings are unsatisfactory. 
 
    them ... death--act as if they did ( Proverbs 8:36 Proverbs 17:19 ).

title: Proverbs 21:7
text:
7. robbery--or, "destruction," especially oppression, of which they are authors. 
 
    shall destroy--literally, "cut with a saw" ( I Kings 7:9 ), that is, utterly ruin them. Their sins shall be visited on them in kind. 
 
    to do judgment--what is just and right.

title: Proverbs 21:8
text: 8. of man--any one; his way is opposed to truth, and also estranged from it. The pure proves himself such by his right conduct.

title: Proverbs 21:9
text:
9. corner--a turret or arbor on the roof. 
 
    brawling--or contentious. 
 
    wide house--literally, "house of fellowship," large enough for several families.

title: Proverbs 21:10
text: 10. So strongly does he desire to do evil ( Psalms 10:3 Ecclesiastes 8:11 ), that he will not even spare his friend if in his way.

title: Proverbs 21:11
text: 11. (Compare  Proverbs 19:25 ). That which the simple learn by the terrors of punishment, the wise learn by teaching.

title: Proverbs 21:12
text:
12. (Compare  Psalms 37:35-38 Psalms 73:17 Psalms 73:20 ). 
 
    house--family or interests. 
 
    overthroweth--either supply "God" (compare  Proverbs 10:24 ), or the word is used impersonally.

title: Proverbs 21:13
text: 13. The principles of retribution, often taught (compare  Psalms 18:26 Matthew 7:1-12 ).

title: Proverbs 21:14
text: 14. The effect of bribery ( Proverbs 17:23 ) is enhanced by secrecy, as the bribed person does not wish his motives made known.

title: Proverbs 21:15
text: 15. But the just love right and need no bribes. The wicked at last meet destruction, though for a time happy in concealing corruption.

title: Proverbs 21:16
text:
16. the way of understanding--(Compare  Proverbs 12:26 Proverbs 14:22 ). 
 
    remain--that is, rest as at a journey's end; death will be his unchanging home.

title: Proverbs 21:17
text: 17. Costly luxuries impoverish.

title: Proverbs 21:18
text: 18. (Compare  Proverbs 11:8 ). By suffering what they had devised for the righteous, or brought on them, the wicked became their ransom, in the usual sense of substitutes (compare  Joshua 7:26 Esther 7:9 ).

title: Proverbs 21:19
text:
19. (Compare  Proverbs 21:9 ). 
 
    wilderness--pasture, though uninhabitable ground ( Psalms 65:12 ).

title: Proverbs 21:20
text:
20. The wise, by diligence and care, lay up and increase wealth, while fools 
 
    spend--literally, "swallow it up," greedily.

title: Proverbs 21:21
text: 21. He who tries to act justly and kindly ( Psalms 34:14 ) will prosper and obtain justice and honor.

title: Proverbs 21:22
text:
22. "Wisdom is better than strength" ( Ecclesiastes 7:19 Ecclesiastes 9:15 ). 
 
    strength ... thereof--that in which they confide.

title: Proverbs 21:23
text: 23. (Compare  Proverbs 13:2 Proverbs 13:3 James 3:6-10 ).

title: Proverbs 21:24
text: 24. The reproachful name is deserved by those who treat others with anger and contempt.

title: Proverbs 21:25
text: 25. desire--that is of ease and idleness brings him to starvation.

title: Proverbs 21:26
text: 26. The sin of covetousness marks the sluggard, as the virtue of benevolence the righteous.

title: Proverbs 21:27
text:
27. God regards the heart, and hypocrisy is more odious than open inconsistency. 
 
    wicked mind--or, "design" ( Proverbs 1:4 ).

title: Proverbs 21:28
text:
28. (Compare  Proverbs 19:5 ). 
 
    that heareth--or heeds instruction, and so grows wise. 
 
    speaketh constantly--or sincerely (compare  Habakkuk 1:5 ), and hence is believed ( Proverbs 12:19 James 1:19 ).

title: Proverbs 21:29
text:
29. hardeneth his face--is obstinate. 
 
    directeth ... way--considers it, and acts advisedly.

title: Proverbs 21:30
text: 30, 31. Men's best devices and reliances are vain compared with God's, or without His aid ( Proverbs 19:21 Psalms 20:7 Psalms 33:17 ).

title: Proverbs 22:1
text:
Proverbs 22:1-29 . 
 
    1. A good name-- ( Job 30:8 , Hebrew); "good" is supplied here from  Ecclesiastes 7:1 . 
 
    loving favour--kind regard, that is, of the wise and good.

title: Proverbs 22:2
text: 2. Before God all are on the same footing ( Proverbs 14:31 Proverbs 17:5 ).

title: Proverbs 22:3
text: 3. are punished--that is, for their temerity; for the evil is not necessarily punitive, as the prudent might otherwise be its objects.

title: Proverbs 22:4
text: 4. humility and the fear of the Lord--are in apposition; one produces the other. On the results, compare  Proverbs 3:16 Proverbs 8:18 .

title: Proverbs 22:5
text: 5. he that ... them--Those who properly watch over their own souls are thus preserved from the dangers which attend the way of perverse men ( Proverbs 16:17 ).

title: Proverbs 22:6
text:
6. Train--initiate, or early instruct. 
 
    the way--literally, "his way," that selected for him in which he should go; for early training secures habitual walking in it.

title: Proverbs 22:7
text: 7. The influence of wealth sets aside moral distinctions is implied, and, of course, disapproved (compare  Proverbs 19:6 Proverbs 21:14 , &c.).

title: Proverbs 22:8
text:
8. (Compare  Proverbs 11:18 Psalms 109:16-20 Galatians 6:7 Galatians 6:8 ). 
 
    the rod ... fail--His power to do evil will be destroyed.

title: Proverbs 22:9
text:
9. a bountiful eye--that is, a beneficent disposition. 
 
    for he giveth ... poor--His acts prove it.

title: Proverbs 22:10
text: 10. Cast out--or drive away. Scorners foster strife by taunts and revilings.

title: Proverbs 22:11
text:
11. (Compare Margin). 
 
    pureness of heart--and gentle, kind words win favor, even from kings.

title: Proverbs 22:12
text:
12. preserve--or guard. 
 
    knowledge--its principles and possessors. 
 
    overthroweth--utterly confounds and destroys the wicked.

title: Proverbs 22:13
text: 13. Frivolous excuses satisfy the indolent man's conscience.

title: Proverbs 22:14
text: 14. The mouth--or flattering speeches ( Proverbs 5:3 Proverbs 7:5 ) ensnare man, as pits, beasts. God makes their own sin their punishment.

title: Proverbs 22:15
text: 15. is bound--or firmly fixed. Chastisement deters from crime and so leads to reformation of principle.

title: Proverbs 22:16
text: 16. These two vices pertain to the same selfish feeling. Both are deservedly odious to God and incur punishment.

title: Proverbs 22:17
text: 17. Here begins another division of the book, marked by those encouragements to the pursuit of wisdom, which are found in the earlier chapters. It will be observed that at  Proverbs 22:22-24:12 , the proverbs are generally expressed in two verses instead of one (see (unresolved link)).

title: Proverbs 22:18
text:
18. These lessons must be laid up in the mind, and 
 
    fitted--or better, "fixed" in the lips so as to be ever ready.

title: Proverbs 22:19
text: 19. That ... Lord--This is the design of the instruction.

title: Proverbs 22:20
text:
20. excellent things--or probably of former times. 
 
    counsels and knowledge--both advice and instruction.

title: Proverbs 22:21
text: 21. Specially he desires to secure accuracy, so that his pupil may teach others.

title: Proverbs 22:22
text:
22, 23. Here follow ten precepts of two verses each. Though men fail to defend the poor, God will ( Proverbs 17:5 Psalms 12:5 ). 
 
    in the gate--place of public gathering ( Job 5:4 Psalms 69:12 ).

title: Proverbs 22:24
text: 24, 25. (Compare  Proverbs 2:12-15 Proverbs 4:14 ).

title: Proverbs 22:25
text: 25. a snare ... soul--The unsuspecting are often misled by bad company.

title: Proverbs 22:26
text: 26, 27. (Compare  Proverbs 6:1 Proverbs 17:18 ).

title: Proverbs 22:27
text: 27. should he take, &c.--that is, the creditor.

title: Proverbs 22:28
text: 28. (Compare  Proverbs 23:10 ). Do not entrench on others ( Deuteronomy 19:14 Deuteronomy 27:17 ).

title: Proverbs 22:29
text: 29. Success rewards diligence ( Proverbs 10:4 Proverbs 21:5 ).

title: Proverbs 23:1
text:
Proverbs 23:1-35 . 
 
    1. Avoid the dangers of gluttony.

title: Proverbs 23:2
text: 2. put a knife--an Eastern figure for putting restraint on the appetite.

title: Proverbs 23:3
text: 3. are deceitful meat--though well tasted, injurious.

title: Proverbs 23:4
text:
4, 5. (Compare  I Timothy 6:9 I Timothy 6:10 ). 
 
    thine own wisdom--which regards riches intrinsically as a blessing.

title: Proverbs 23:5
text: 5. Wilt ... eyes--As the eyes fly after or seek riches, they are not, that is, either become transitory or unsatisfying; fully expressed by their flying away.

title: Proverbs 23:6
text:
6-8. Beware of deceitful men, whose courtesies even you will repent of having accepted. 
 
    evil eye--or purpose ( Proverbs 22:9 Deuteronomy 15:9 Matthew 6:23 ).

title: Proverbs 23:8
text: 8. The morsel ... words--that is, disgusted with his true character, all pleasant intercourse will be destroyed.

title: Proverbs 23:9
text: 9. (Compare  Proverbs 9:8 ). "Cast not your pearls before swine" ( Matthew 7:6 ).

title: Proverbs 23:10
text: 10, 11. (Compare  Proverbs 22:22 Proverbs 22:23 ).

title: Proverbs 23:11
text:
11. redeemer--or avenger ( Leviticus 25:25 Leviticus 25:26 Numbers 35:12 ), hence advocate ( Job 19:25 ). 
 
    plead ... thee--(Compare  Job 31:21 Psalms 35:1 Psalms 68:5 ).

title: Proverbs 23:12
text: 12. Here begins another series of precepts.

title: Proverbs 23:13
text: 13, 14. While there is little danger that the use of the "divine ordinance of the rod" will produce bodily harm, there is great hope of spiritual good.

title: Proverbs 23:15
text: 15. 16. The pleasure afforded the teacher by the pupil's progress is a motive to diligence.

title: Proverbs 23:16
text: 16. my reins--(Compare  Psalms 7:9 ).

title: Proverbs 23:17
text: 17, 18. (Compare Margin). The prosperity of the wicked is short.

title: Proverbs 23:18
text: 18. an end--or, "hereafter," another time, when apparent inequalities shall be adjusted (compare  Psalms 37:28-38 ).

title: Proverbs 23:19
text: 19-21. guide ... way--or direct thy thoughts to a right course of conduct (compare  Proverbs 4:4 Proverbs 9:6 ).

title: Proverbs 23:20
text: 20. riotous ... flesh--prodigal, or eating more than necessary. Instead of "their flesh" (compare Margin), better, "flesh to them," that is, used for pleasure.

title: Proverbs 23:21
text: 21. drowsiness--the dreamy sleep of the slothful.

title: Proverbs 23:22
text:
22. Hearken--that is, obey ( Proverbs 1:8 Ephesians 6:1 ). 
 
    despise ... old--Adults revere the parents whom, as children, they once obeyed.

title: Proverbs 23:23
text:
23. Buy--literally, "get" ( Proverbs 4:5 ). 
 
    truth--generally and specially as opposed to errors of all kinds.

title: Proverbs 23:24
text: 24, 25. (Compare  Proverbs 10:1 Proverbs 17:21 Proverbs 17:25 ).

title: Proverbs 23:26
text:
26-35. A solemn warning against whoredom and drunkenness ( Hosea 4:11 ). 
 
    give me--This is the address of that divine wisdom so often presented ( Proverbs 8:1 Proverbs 9:3 , &c.). 
 
    heart--confidence. 
 
    observe--keep. 
 
    my ways--such as I teach you ( Proverbs 3:17 Proverbs 9:6 ).

title: Proverbs 23:27
text:
27, 28. deep ditch--a narrow pit, out of which it is hard to climb. 
 
    lieth in wait--to ensnare men into the pit, as hunters entrap game (compare  Proverbs 22:14 ).

title: Proverbs 23:28
text: 28. increaseth ... transgressors-- ( Proverbs 5:8-10 ). The vice alluded to is peculiarly hardening to the heart.

title: Proverbs 23:29
text:
29, 30. This picture is often sadly realized now. 
 
    mixed wine--(Compare  Proverbs 9:2 Isaiah 5:11 ).

title: Proverbs 23:31
text:
31. when ... red--the color denoting greater strength (compare  Genesis 49:11 Deuteronomy 32:14 ). 
 
    giveth ... cup--literally, "gives its eye," that is, sparkles. 
 
    moveth ... aright--Perhaps its foaming is meant.

title: Proverbs 23:32
text: 32. The acute miseries resulting from drunkenness contrasted with the temptations.

title: Proverbs 23:33
text: 33, 34. The moral effects: it inflames passion ( Genesis 19:31 Genesis 19:35 ), lays open the heart, produces insensibility to the greatest dangers, and debars from reformation, under the severest sufferings.

title: Proverbs 23:35
text: 35. awake--that is, from drunkenness ( Genesis 9:24 ). This is the language rather of acts than of the tongue.

title: Proverbs 24:1
text:
Proverbs 24:1-34 . 
 
    1, 2. (Compare  Proverbs 23:3 Proverbs 23:17 Psalms 37:1 ).

title: Proverbs 24:2
text:
2. studieth--meditateth. 
 
    talk ... mischief--Their expressed purposes are to do evil.

title: Proverbs 24:3
text:
3, 4. (Compare  Proverbs 14:1 Isaiah 54:14 ). 
 
    house--including the family.

title: Proverbs 24:4
text: 4. by knowledge ... riches-- ( Proverbs 8:18 Proverbs 21:20 ).

title: Proverbs 24:5
text: 5, 6. The general statement ( Ecclesiastes 9:16 Ecclesiastes 9:18 ) is specially illustrated (compare  Proverbs 21:22 Psalms 144:1 ).

title: Proverbs 24:7
text:
7. (Compare  Proverbs 14:16 ). 
 
    in the gate--(Compare  Proverbs 22:22 ).

title: Proverbs 24:8
text: 8. So called even if he fails to do evil.

title: Proverbs 24:9
text: 9. Same thought varied.

title: Proverbs 24:10
text: 10. Literally, "If thou fail in the day of straits (adversity), strait (or, small) is thy strength," which is then truly tested.

title: Proverbs 24:11
text:
11, 12. Neglect of known duty is sin ( James 4:17 ). 
 
    ready--literally, "bowing down" 
 
    to be slain--that is, unjustly. God's retributive justice cannot be avoided by professed ignorance.

title: Proverbs 24:13
text: 13, 14. As delicious food whets the appetite, so should the rewards of wisdom excite us to seek it.

title: Proverbs 24:14
text: 14. reward--literally, "after part," the proper result (compare  Proverbs 23:18 Psalms 37:37 Psalms 37:38 ).

title: Proverbs 24:15
text: 15, 16. The plots of the wicked against the good, though partially, shall not be fully successful ( Psalms 37:24 ); while the wicked, falling under penal evil, find no help.

title: Proverbs 24:16
text: 16. seven times--often, or many ( Proverbs 6:16 Proverbs 6:31 Proverbs 9:1 ).

title: Proverbs 24:17
text: 17, 18. Yet let none rejoice over the fate of evildoers, lest God punish their wrong spirit by relieving the sufferer (compare  Proverbs 17:5 Job 31:29 ).

title: Proverbs 24:19
text: 19, 20. ( Psalms 37:1 Psalms 37:38 Psalms 18:28 ).

title: Proverbs 24:20
text: 20. candle--or, "prosperity"; it shall come to an end ( Proverbs 13:9 Proverbs 20:20 ).

title: Proverbs 24:21
text:
21, 22. A warning against impiety and resistance to lawful rule ( Romans 13:1-7 I Peter 2:17 ). 
 
    meddle ... change--(Compare Margin), literally, "mingle not yourself," avoid the society of restless persons.

title: Proverbs 24:22
text: 22. their calamity, &c.--either what God and the king inflict, or what changers and their company suffer; better the first.

title: Proverbs 24:23
text:
23. These ... wise--literally, "are of the wise," as authors (compare "Psalms of David," Hebrew). "These" refers to the verses following,  Proverbs 24:24-34 . 
 
    to have respect--literally, "to discern faces," show partiality,

title: Proverbs 24:24
text: 24, 25. of which an example is justifying the wicked, to which is opposed, rebuking him, which has a blessing.

title: Proverbs 24:26
text:
26. kiss his lips--love and obey, do homage ( Psalms 2:12 Song of Solomon 8:1 ). 
 
    right answer--literally, "plain words" (compare  Proverbs 8:9 ), opposed to deceptive, or obscure.

title: Proverbs 24:27
text: 27. Prepare ... in the field--Secure, by diligence, a proper support, and then build; provide necessaries, then comforts, to which a house rather pertained, in a mild climate, permitting the use of tents.

title: Proverbs 24:28
text: 28. Do not speak even truth needlessly against any, and never falsehood.

title: Proverbs 24:29
text: 29. Especially avoid retaliation ( Matthew 5:43-45 Romans 12:17 ).

title: Proverbs 24:30
text: 30, 31. A striking picture of the effects of sloth.

title: Proverbs 24:32
text: 32-34. From the folly of the sluggard learn wisdom ( Proverbs 6:10 Proverbs 6:11 ).

title: Proverbs 25:1
text:
Proverbs 25:1-28 . 
 
    1. The character of these proverbs sustains the title (see (unresolved link)). 
 
    also--refers to the former part of the book. 
 
    copied out--literally, "transferred," that is, from some other book to this; not given from memory.

title: Proverbs 25:2
text: 2. God's unsearchableness impresses us with awe (compare  Isaiah 45:15 Romans 11:33 ). But kings, being finite, should confer with wise counsellors;

title: Proverbs 25:3
text: 3. Ye wisely keeping state secrets, which to common men are as inaccessible heights and depths.

title: Proverbs 25:4
text: 4, 5. As separating impurities from ore leaves pure silver, so taking from a king wicked counsellors leaves a wise and beneficent government.

title: Proverbs 25:5
text: 5. before--or, "in presence of," as courtiers stood about a king.

title: Proverbs 25:6
text: 6, 7. Do not intrude into the presence of the king, for the elevation of the humble is honorable, but the humbling of the proud disgraceful ( Luke 14:8-10 ).

title: Proverbs 25:8
text:
8. (Compare  Proverbs 3:30 ). 
 
    lest ... shame--lest you do what you ought not, when shamed by defeat, or "lest thou art shut out from doing any thing."

title: Proverbs 25:9
text:
9, 10. (Compare  Matthew 5:25 , Margin). 
 
    secret--that is, of your opponent, for his disadvantage, and so you be disgraced, not having discussed your difficulties with him.

title: Proverbs 25:11
text:
11. a word fitly--literally, "quickly," as wheels roll, just in time. The comparison as apples ... silver gives a like sense. 
 
    apples, &c.--either real apples of golden color, in a silver network basket, or imitations on silver embroidery.

title: Proverbs 25:12
text: 12. Those who desire to know and do rightly, most highly esteem good counsel ( Proverbs 9:9 Proverbs 15:31 ). The listening ear is better than one hung with gold.

title: Proverbs 25:13
text: 13. Snow from mountains was used to cool drinks; so refreshing is a faithful messenger ( Proverbs 13:17 ).

title: Proverbs 25:14
text:
14. clouds--literally, "vapors" ( Jeremiah 10:13 ), clouds only in appearance. 
 
    a false gift--promised, but not given.

title: Proverbs 25:15
text:
15. Gentleness and kindness overcome the most powerful and obstinate. 
 
    long forbearing--or, "slowness to anger" ( Proverbs 14:29 Proverbs 15:18 ).

title: Proverbs 25:16
text: 16, 17. A comparison, as a surfeit of honey produces physical disgust, so your company, however agreeable in moderation, may, if excessive, lead your friend to hate you.

title: Proverbs 25:18
text:
18. A false witness is as destructive to reputation, as such weapons to the body ( Proverbs 24:28 ). 
 
    beareth ... witness--literally, "answereth questions," as before a judge, against his neighbor.

title: Proverbs 25:19
text: 19. Treachery annoys as well as deceives.

title: Proverbs 25:20
text: 20. Not only is the incongruity of songs (that is, joyful) and sadness meant, but an accession of sadness, by want of sympathy, is implied.

title: Proverbs 25:21
text: 21, 22. (Compare  Matthew 5:44 Romans 12:20 ). As metals are melted by heaping coals upon them, so is the heart softened by kindness.

title: Proverbs 25:23
text: 23. Better, "As the north wind bringeth forth ( Psalms 90:2 ) or produces rain, so does a concealed or slandering tongue produce anger."

title: Proverbs 25:24
text: 24. (Compare  Proverbs 21:9 Proverbs 21:19 ).

title: Proverbs 25:25
text:
25. (Compare  Proverbs 25:13 ). 
 
    good news--that is, of some loved interest or absent friend, the more grateful as coming from afar.

title: Proverbs 25:26
text: 26. From troubled fountains and corrupt springs no healthy water is to be had, so when the righteous are oppressed by the wicked, their power for good is lessened or destroyed.

title: Proverbs 25:27
text:
27. Satiety surfeits ( Proverbs 25:16 ); so men who are self-glorious find shame. 
 
    is not glory--"not" is supplied from the first clause, or "is grievous," in which sense a similar word is used ( Proverbs 27:2 ).

title: Proverbs 25:28
text: 28. Such are exposed to the incursions of evil thoughts and successful temptations.

title: Proverbs 26:1
text:
Proverbs 26:1-28 . 
 
    1. The incongruities of nature illustrate also those of the moral world. The fool's unworthiness is also implied ( Proverbs 17:7 Proverbs 19:10 ).

title: Proverbs 26:2
text:
2. Though not obvious to us, 
 
    the bird--literally, "sparrow"--and 
 
    swallow--have an object in their motions, so penal evil falls on none without a reason.

title: Proverbs 26:3
text: 3. The rod is as much needed by fools and as well suited to them, as whips and bridles are for beasts.

title: Proverbs 26:4
text: 4, 5. Answer not--that is, approvingly by like folly.

title: Proverbs 26:5
text: 5. Answer--by reproof.

title: Proverbs 26:6
text:
6. A fool fails by folly as surely as if he were maimed. 
 
    drinketh damage--that is, gets it abundantly ( Job 15:16 Job 34:7 ).

title: Proverbs 26:7
text: 7. legs ... equal--or, "take away the legs," or "the legs ... are weak." In any case the idea is that they are the occasion of an awkwardness, such as the fool shows in using a parable or proverb (see (unresolved link);  Proverbs 17:7 ).

title: Proverbs 26:8
text: 8. A stone, bound in a sling, is useless; so honor, conferred on a fool, is thrown away.

title: Proverbs 26:9
text: 9. As vexatious and unmanageable as a thorn in a drunkard's hand is a parable to a fool. He will be as apt to misuse is as to use it rightly.

title: Proverbs 26:10
text:
10. Various versions of this are proposed (Compare Margin). Better perhaps--"Much He injures (or literally, "wounds") all who reward," &c., that is, society is injured by encouraging evil men. 
 
    transgressors--may be rendered "vagrants." The word "God" is improperly supplied.

title: Proverbs 26:11
text: 11. returneth ... folly--Though disgusting to others, the fool delights in his folly.

title: Proverbs 26:12
text: 12. The self-conceited are taught with more difficulty than the stupid.

title: Proverbs 26:13
text: 13. (Compare  Proverbs 22:13 ).

title: Proverbs 26:14
text: 14. (Compare  Proverbs 6:10 Proverbs 24:33 ).

title: Proverbs 26:15
text: 15. (Compare  Proverbs 19:24 ).

title: Proverbs 26:16
text: 16. The thoughtless being ignorant of their ignorance are conceited.

title: Proverbs 26:17
text: 17. meddleth--as in  Proverbs 20:19 Proverbs 24:21 ; as either holding a dog by the ears or letting him go involves danger, so success in another man's strife or failure involves a useless risk of reputation, does no good, and may do us harm.

title: Proverbs 26:18
text: 18, 19. Such are reckless of results.

title: Proverbs 26:20
text: 20, 21. The talebearers foster ( Proverbs 16:28 ), and the contentious excite, strife.

title: Proverbs 26:22
text: 22. (Compare  Proverbs 18:8 ).

title: Proverbs 26:23
text: 23. Warm professions can no more give value to insincerity than silver coating to rude earthenware.

title: Proverbs 26:24
text: 24. dissembleth--though an unusual sense of the word (compare Margin), is allowable, and better suits the context, which sets forth hypocrisy.

title: Proverbs 26:25
text:
25. Sentiment of  Proverbs 26:24  carried out. 
 
    seven abominations in his heart--that is, very many (compare  Proverbs 24:16 ).

title: Proverbs 26:26
text: 26, 27. Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare  Proverbs 12:13 Psalms 7:16 Psalms 9:17 , &c.).

title: Proverbs 26:28
text:
28. Men hate those they injure. 
 
    A lying tongue--"lips" for the persons (compare  Proverbs 4:24 Psalms 12:3 ).

title: Proverbs 27:1
text:
Proverbs 27:1-27 . 
 
    1. Do not confide implicitly in your plans ( Proverbs 16:9 Proverbs 19:21 James 4:13-15 ).

title: Proverbs 27:2
text: 2. Avoid self-praise.

title: Proverbs 27:3
text:
3. heavy--The literal sense of "heavy," applied to material subjects, illustrates its figurative, "grievous," applied to moral. 
 
    a fool's wrath--is unreasonable and excessive.

title: Proverbs 27:4
text: 4. envy--or, "jealousy" (compare Margin;  Proverbs 6:34 ), is more unappeasable than the simpler bad passions.

title: Proverbs 27:5
text: 5, 6. secret love--not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.

title: Proverbs 27:7
text: 7. The luxury of wealth confers less happiness than the healthy appetite of labor.

title: Proverbs 27:8
text: 8. Such are not only out of place, but out of duty and in danger.

title: Proverbs 27:9
text:
9. rejoice the heart--the organ of perceiving what pleases the senses. 
 
    sweetness ... counsel--or, "wise counsel is also pleasing."

title: Proverbs 27:10
text: 10. Adhere to tried friends. The ties of blood may be less reliable than those of genuine friendship.

title: Proverbs 27:11
text: 11. The wisdom of children both reflects credit on parents and contributes to their aid in difficulties.

title: Proverbs 27:12
text: 12, 13. (Compare  Proverbs 20:16 Proverbs 22:3 ).

title: Proverbs 27:14
text: 14. Excessive zeal in praising raises suspicions of selfishness.

title: Proverbs 27:15
text:
15. (Compare  Proverbs 19:13 ). 
 
    very ... day--literally "a day of showers."

title: Proverbs 27:16
text:
16. hideth--or, "restrains" (that is, tries to do it); is as fruitless an effort, as that of holding the wind. 
 
    the ointment of his right hand--the organ of power ( Psalms 17:7 Psalms 18:35 ). His right hand endeavors to repress perfume, but vainly. Some prefer: "His right hand comes on oil," that is, "cannot take hold." Such a woman cannot be tamed.

title: Proverbs 27:17
text: 17. a man sharpeneth ... friend--that is, conversation promotes intelligence, which the face exhibits.

title: Proverbs 27:18
text: 18. Diligence secures a reward, even for the humble servant.

title: Proverbs 27:19
text: 19. We may see our characters in the developed tempers of others.

title: Proverbs 27:20
text: 20. Men's cupidity is as insatiable as the grave.

title: Proverbs 27:21
text:
21. Praise tests character. 
 
    a man to his praise--according to his praise, as he bears it. Thus vain men seek it, weak men are inflated by it, wise men disregard it, &c.

title: Proverbs 27:22
text: 22. The obstinate wickedness of such is incurable by the heaviest inflictions.

title: Proverbs 27:23
text: 23, 24. flocks--constituted the staple of wealth. It is only by care and diligence that the most solid possessions can be perpetuated ( Proverbs 23:5 ).

title: Proverbs 27:25
text:
25-27. The fact that providential arrangements furnish the means of competence to those who properly use them is another motive to diligence (compare  Psalms 65:9-13 ). 
 
    The hay appeareth--literally, "Grass appeareth" ( Job 40:15 Psalms 104:14 ).

title: Proverbs 27:27
text: 27. household--literally, "house," the family ( Acts 16:15 I Corinthians 1:16 ).

title: Proverbs 28:1
text:
Proverbs 28:1-28 . 
 
    1. A bad conscience makes men timid; the righteous are alone truly bold ( Proverbs 14:26 Psalms 27:1 ).

title: Proverbs 28:2
text:
2. Anarchy producing contending rulers shortens the reign of each. 
 
    but by a man ... prolonged--or, "by a man of understanding--that is, a good ruler--he who knows or regards the right, that is, a good citizen, shall prolong (his days)." Good rulers are a blessing to the people. Bad government as a punishment for evil is contrasted with good as blessing to the good.

title: Proverbs 28:3
text: 3. A poor man, &c.--Such, in power, exact more severely, and so leave subjects bare.

title: Proverbs 28:4
text: 4. They that forsake ... wicked--Wrongdoers encourage one another.

title: Proverbs 28:5
text: 5. (Compare  John 7:17 ). Ignorance of moral truth is due to unwillingness to know it.

title: Proverbs 28:6
text: 6. (Compare  Proverbs 10:6 ). Riches cannot compensate for sin, nor the want of them affect integrity.

title: Proverbs 28:7
text:
7. (Compare  Proverbs 17:25 ). 
 
    riotous men--or, "gluttons" ( Proverbs 23:20 Proverbs 23:21 ).

title: Proverbs 28:8
text: 8. usury ... unjust gain--(Compare Margin). The two terms, meaning nearly the same, may denote excessive interest. God's providence directs the proper use of wealth.

title: Proverbs 28:9
text:
9. (Compare  Proverbs 15:8 Proverbs 21:27 ). 
 
    hearing--that is, obeying. God requires sincere worshippers ( Psalms 66:18 John 4:24 ).

title: Proverbs 28:10
text: 10. (Compare  Proverbs 26:27 ).

title: Proverbs 28:11
text: 11. A poor but wise man can discover (and expose) the rich and self-conceited.

title: Proverbs 28:12
text:
12. great glory--or, cause for it to a people, for the righteous rejoice in good, and righteousness exalts a nation ( Proverbs 14:34 ). 
 
    a man ... hidden--that is, the good retire, or all kinds try to escape a wicked rule.

title: Proverbs 28:13
text: 13. (Compare  Psalms 32:3-5 ). Concealment of sin delivers none from God's wrath, but He shows mercy to the humble penitent ( Psalms 51:4 ).

title: Proverbs 28:14
text:
14. feareth--that is, God, and so repents. 
 
    hardeneth his heart--makes himself insensible to sin, and so will not repent ( Proverbs 14:16 Proverbs 29:1 ).

title: Proverbs 28:15
text: 15. The rapacity and cruelty of such beasts well represent some wicked men (compare  Psalms 7:2 Psalms 17:12 ).

title: Proverbs 28:16
text: 16. The prince ... understanding--that is, He does not perceive that oppression jeopards his success. Covetousness often produces oppression, hence the contrast.

title: Proverbs 28:17
text:
17. doeth violence ... blood, &c.--or, that is oppressed by the blood of life ( Genesis 9:6 ), which he has taken. 
 
    to the pit--the grave or destruction ( Proverbs 1:12 Job 33:18-24 Psalms 143:7 ). 
 
    stay him--sustain or deliver him.

title: Proverbs 28:18
text: 18. (Compare  Proverbs 10:9 Proverbs 17:20 ). Double dealing is eventually fatal.

title: Proverbs 28:19
text:
19. (Compare  Proverbs 10:4 Proverbs 20:4 ). 
 
    vain persons--idle, useless drones, implying that they are also wicked ( Proverbs 12:11 Psalms 26:4 ).

title: Proverbs 28:20
text: 20. maketh haste ... rich--implying deceit or fraud ( Proverbs 20:21 ), and so opposed to "faithful" or reliable.

title: Proverbs 28:21
text: 21. respect of persons-- ( Proverbs 24:23 ). Such are led to evil by the slightest motive.

title: Proverbs 28:22
text:
22. (Compare  Proverbs 28:20 ). 
 
    evil eye--in the general sense of  Proverbs 23:6 , here more specific for covetousness (compare  Proverbs 22:9 Matthew 20:15 ). 
 
    poverty ... him--by God's providence.

title: Proverbs 28:23
text: 23. (Compare  Proverbs 9:8 Proverbs 9:9 Proverbs 27:5 ). Those benefited by reproof will love their monitors.

title: Proverbs 28:24
text: 24. (Compare  Matthew 15:4-6 ). Such, though heirs, are virtually thieves, to be ranked with highwaymen.

title: Proverbs 28:25
text:
25. of a proud heart--literally, "puffed up of soul"--that is, self-confident, and hence overbearing and litigious. 
 
    made fat--or, "prosperous" ( Proverbs 11:25 Proverbs 16:20 ).

title: Proverbs 28:26
text:
26. (Compare  Proverbs 3:6-8 ). 
 
    walketh wisely--that is, trusting in God ( Proverbs 22:17-19 ).

title: Proverbs 28:27
text:
27. (Compare  Proverbs 11:24-26 ). 
 
    hideth his eyes--as the face ( Psalms 27:9 Psalms 69:17 ), denotes inattention.

title: Proverbs 28:28
text: 28. The elevation of the wicked to power drives men to seek refuge from tyranny (compare  Proverbs 28:12 Proverbs 11:10 Psalms 12:8 ).

title: Proverbs 29:1
text:
Proverbs 29:1-27 . 
 
    1. hardeneth ... neck--obstinately refuses counsel ( II Kings 17:14 Nehemiah 9:16 ). 
 
    destroyed--literally, "shivered" or "utterly broken to pieces." 
 
    without remedy--literally, "without healing" or repairing.

title: Proverbs 29:2
text:
2. (Compare  Proverbs 11:10 Proverbs 28:28 ). 
 
    in authority--(Compare Margin), increased in power.

title: Proverbs 29:3
text: 3. (Compare  Proverbs 4:6 Proverbs 4:7 Proverbs 10:1 , &c.).

title: Proverbs 29:4
text:
4. by judgment--that is, righteous decisions, opposed to those procured by gifts (compare  Proverbs 28:21 ), by which good government is perverted. 
 
    land--for nation.

title: Proverbs 29:5
text:
5. (Compare  Proverbs 26:28 ). 
 
    spreadeth ... feet--By misleading him as to his real character, the flatterer brings him to evil, prepared by himself or others.

title: Proverbs 29:6
text:
6. In--or, "By" 
 
    the transgression--he is brought into difficulty ( Proverbs 12:13 ), but the righteous go on prospering, and so sing or rejoice.

title: Proverbs 29:7
text:
7. considereth--literally, "knows," as  Psalms 1:6 . 
 
    the cause--that is, in courts of justice (compare  Proverbs 29:14 ). The voluntary neglect of it by the wicked ( Proverbs 28:27 ) occasions oppression.

title: Proverbs 29:8
text:
8. Scornful men--those who contemptuously disregard God's law. 
 
    bring--(Compare Margin), kindle strife. 
 
    turn away wrath--that is, "abate wrath."

title: Proverbs 29:9
text:
9. contendeth--that is, in law. 
 
    whether ... laugh--The fool, whether angry or good-humored, is unsettled; or referring the words to the wise man, the sense is, that all his efforts, severe or gentle, are unavailing to pacify the fool.

title: Proverbs 29:10
text:
10. bloodthirsty--(Compare Margin), murderers ( Psalms 5:6 Psalms 26:9 ). 
 
    hate, &c.-- ( Proverbs 1:11 Genesis 3:4 ). 
 
    seek ... soul--that is, to preserve it.

title: Proverbs 29:11
text:
11. (Compare  Proverbs 12:16 Proverbs 16:32 ). 
 
    mind--or, "spirit," for anger or any ill passion which the righteous restrain.

title: Proverbs 29:12
text: 12. His servants imitate him.

title: Proverbs 29:13
text:
13. (Compare  Proverbs 22:2 ). 
 
    deceitful man--literally, "man of vexations," an exactor. 
 
    the Lord ... their eyes--sustains their lives ( I Samuel 14:27 Psalms 13:3 ); that is, both depend on Him, and He will do justice.

title: Proverbs 29:14
text: 14. (Compare  Proverbs 20:28 Proverbs 25:5 ). Such is the character of the King of kings ( Psalms 72:4 Psalms 72:12 ).

title: Proverbs 29:15
text: 15. (Compare  Proverbs 13:24 Proverbs 23:13 ).

title: Proverbs 29:16
text:
16. (Compare  Proverbs 29:2 Proverbs 29:12 Psalms 12:1-8 ). 
 
    shall see ... fall--and triumph in it ( Psalms 37:34-38 Psalms 58:10 Psalms 58:11 ).

title: Proverbs 29:17
text:
17. (Compare  Proverbs 29:3 Proverbs 29:15 Proverbs 19:18 ). 
 
    give thee rest--peace and quiet (compare  Proverbs 29:9 ).

title: Proverbs 29:18
text:
18. no vision--instruction in God's truth, which was by prophets, through visions ( I Samuel 3:1 ). 
 
    people perish--(Compare Margin), are deprived of moral restraints. 
 
    keepeth the law--has, and observes, instruction ( Proverbs 14:11 Proverbs 14:34 Psalms 19:11 ).

title: Proverbs 29:19
text:
19. A servant--who lacks good principle. 
 
    corrected--or discovered. 
 
    will not answer--that is, will not obey.

title: Proverbs 29:20
text:
20. (Compare  Proverbs 21:5 ). 
 
    hasty in ... words?--implying self-conceit ( Proverbs 26:12 ).

title: Proverbs 29:21
text: 21. become his son--assume the place and privileges of one.

title: Proverbs 29:22
text: 22. (Compare  Proverbs 15:18 ). Such are delighted by discord and violence.

title: Proverbs 29:23
text:
23. (Compare  Proverbs 16:18 Proverbs 18:12 ). 
 
    honour ... spirit--or, "such shall lay hold on honor" ( Proverbs 11:16 ).

title: Proverbs 29:24
text:
24. hateth ... soul--(Compare  Proverbs 8:36 ). 
 
    heareth cursing-- ( Leviticus 5:1 ), risks the punishment, rather than reveal truth.

title: Proverbs 29:25
text:
25. The fear ... snare--involves men in difficulty (compare  Proverbs 29:6 ). 
 
    shall be safe--(Compare Margin;  Proverbs 18:10 ).

title: Proverbs 29:26
text: 26. (Compare Margin;  Psalms 27:8 ). God alone will and can do exact justice.

title: Proverbs 29:27
text: 27. (Compare  Proverbs 3:32 ). On last clause, compare  Proverbs 29:16 Psalms 37:12 .

title: Proverbs 30:1
text:
Proverbs 30:1-33 . 
 
    1. This is the title of this chapter (see (unresolved link)). 
 
    the prophecy--literally, "the burden" (compare  Isaiah 13:1 Zechariah 9:1 ), used for any divine instruction; not necessarily a prediction, which was only a kind of prophecy ( I Chronicles 15:27 , "a song"). Prophets were inspired men, who spoke for God to man, or for man to God ( Genesis 20:7 Exodus 7:14 Exodus 7:15 Exodus 7:16 ). Such, also, were the New Testament prophets. In a general sense, Gad, Nathan, and others were such, who were divine teachers, though we do not learn that they ever predicted. 
 
    the man spake--literally, "the saying of the man"; an expression used to denote any solemn and important announcement (compare  II Samuel 23:1 Psalms 36:1 Psalms 110:1 Isaiah 1:24 , &c.). Ithiel and Ucal were perhaps pupils.

title: Proverbs 30:2
text: 2-4. brutish-- stupid, a strong term to denote his lowly self-estimation; or he may speak of such as his natural condition, as contrasted with God's all-seeing comprehensive knowledge and almighty power. The questions of this clause emphatically deny the attributes mentioned to be those of any creature, thus impressively strengthening the implied reference of the former to God (compare  Deuteronomy 30:12-14 Isaiah 40:12 Ephesians 4:8 ).

title: Proverbs 30:5
text: 5. (Compare  Psalms 12:6 Psalms 119:140 ).

title: Proverbs 30:6
text:
6. Add ... words--implying that his sole reliance was on God's all-sufficient teaching. 
 
    reprove thee--or, "convict thee"--and so the falsehood will appear.

title: Proverbs 30:7
text: 7-9. A prayer for exemption from wickedness, and the extremes of poverty and riches, the two things mentioned. Contentment is implied as desired.

title: Proverbs 30:8
text: 8. vanity--all sorts of sinful acts ( Job 11:11 Isaiah 5:18 ).

title: Proverbs 30:9
text:
9. be full ... deny-- that is, puffed up by the pride of prosperity. 
 
    take the name ... vain-- This is not (Hebrew) the form (compare  Exodus 20:7 ), but "take" rather denotes laying violent hold on any thing; that is lest I assail God's name or attributes, as justice, mercy, &c., which the poor are tempted to do.

title: Proverbs 30:10
text:
10. Accuse not--Slander not ( Psalms 10:7 ). 
 
    curse ... guilty--lest, however lowly, he be exasperated to turn on thee, and your guilt be made to appear.

title: Proverbs 30:11
text: 11-14. Four kinds of hateful persons--(1) graceless children, (2) hypocrites, (3) the proud, (4) cruel oppressors (compare on  Proverbs 30:14 Psalms 14:4 Psalms 52:2 ) --are now illustrated; (1)  Proverbs 30:15 Proverbs 30:16 , the insatiability of prodigal children and their fate; (2)  Proverbs 30:17 , hypocrisy, or the concealment of real character; (3 and 4)  Proverbs 30:18-20 , various examples of pride and oppression.

title: Proverbs 30:15
text:
15, 16. horse leech--supposed by some to be the vampire (a fabulous creature), as being literally insatiable; but the other subjects mentioned must be taken as this, comparatively insatiable. The use of a fabulous creature agreeably to popular notions is not inconsistent with inspiration. 
 
    There are three ... yea, four--(Compare  Proverbs 6:16 ).

title: Proverbs 30:17
text:
17. The eye--for the person, with reference to the use of the organ to express mockery and contempt, and also as that by which punishment is received. 
 
    the ravens ... eagles ... eat-- either as dying unnaturally, or being left unburied, or both.

title: Proverbs 30:18
text: 18-20. Hypocrisy is illustrated by four examples of the concealment of all methods or traces of action, and a pertinent example of double dealing in actual vice is added, that is, the adulterous woman.

title: Proverbs 30:20
text: 20. she eateth ... mouth--that is, she hides the evidences of her shame and professes innocence.

title: Proverbs 30:21
text: 21-23. Pride and cruelty, the undue exaltation of those unfit to hold power, produce those vices which disquiet society (compare  Proverbs 19:10 Proverbs 28:3 ).

title: Proverbs 30:23
text: 23. heir ... mistress--that is, takes her place as a wife ( Genesis 16:4 ).

title: Proverbs 30:24
text: 24-31. These verses provide two classes of apt illustrations of various aspects of the moral world, which the reader is left to apply. By the first ( Proverbs 30:25-28 ), diligence and providence are commended; the success of these insignificant animals being due to their instinctive sagacity and activity, rather than strength. The other class ( Proverbs 30:30 Proverbs 30:31 ) provides similes for whatever is majestic or comely, uniting efficiency with gracefulness.

title: Proverbs 30:26
text: 26. conies--mountain mice, or rabbits.

title: Proverbs 30:28
text:
28. spider--tolerated, even in palaces, to destroy flies. 
 
    taketh ... hands--or, uses with activity the limbs provided for taking prey.

title: Proverbs 30:32
text:
32. As none can hope, successfully, to resist such a king, suppress even the thought of an attempt. 
 
    lay ... hand upon thy mouth--"lay" is well supplied ( Judges 18:19 Job 29:9 Job 40:4 ).

title: Proverbs 30:33
text: 33. or other ills, as surely arise from devising evil as natural effects from natural causes.

title: Proverbs 31:1
text:
Proverbs 31:1-31 . 
 
    1. On the title of this, the sixth part of the book, see (unresolved link). 
 
    prophecy--(See on  Proverbs 29:27 ).

title: Proverbs 31:2
text:
2. What, my son?--that is, What shall I say? Repetitions denote earnestness. 
 
    son of my womb--as our phrase, "my own son," a term of special affection. 
 
    son of my vows--as one dedicated to God; so the word "Lemuel" may mean.

title: Proverbs 31:3
text:
3-9. Succinct but solemn warnings against vices to which kings are peculiarly tempted, as carnal pleasures and oppressive and unrighteous government are used to sustain sensual indulgence. 
 
    strength-- mental and bodily resources for health and comfort. 
 
    thy ways--or course of life. 
 
    to that ... kings--literally, "to the destroying of kings," avoid destructive pleasures (compare  Proverbs 5:9 Proverbs 7:22 Proverbs 7:27 Hosea 4:11 ).

title: Proverbs 31:4
text:
4, 5. Stimulants enfeeble reason, pervert the heart, and do not suit rulers, who need clear and steady minds, and well-governed affections (compare  Proverbs 20:1 Proverbs 22:29 ). 
 
    pervert ... afflicted--They give unrighteous decisions against the poor.

title: Proverbs 31:6
text: 6, 7. The proper use of such drinks is to restore tone to feeble bodies and depressed minds (compare  Psalms 104:15 ).

title: Proverbs 31:8
text:
8, 9. Open ... cause--Plead for those who cannot plead for themselves, as the orphan, stranger, &c. (compare  Psalms 72:12 Isaiah 1:17 ). 
 
    appointed to destruction--who are otherwise ruined by their oppressors (compare  Proverbs 29:14 Proverbs 29:16 ).

title: Proverbs 31:10
text:
10-31. This exquisite picture of a truly lovely wife is conceived and drawn in accordance with the customs of Eastern nations, but its moral teachings suit all climes. In Hebrew the verses begin with the letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order (compare (unresolved link) to Poetical Books). 
 
    Who ... woman--The question implies that such are rare, though not entirely wanting (compare  Proverbs 18:22 Proverbs 19:14 ). 
 
    virtuous--literally, "of strength," that is, moral courage (compare  Proverbs 12:4 Ruth 3:11 ). 
 
    her price, &c.--(compare  Proverbs 3:15 ).

title: Proverbs 31:11
text:
11. heart ... trust in her--He relies on her prudence and skill. 
 
    no need of spoil--does not lack profit or gain, especially, that obtained by the risk of war.

title: Proverbs 31:12
text: 12. do ... good--contribute good to him.

title: Proverbs 31:13
text: 13, 14. Ancient women of rank thus wrought with their hands; and such, indeed, were the customs of Western women a few centuries since. In the East also, the fabrics were articles of merchandise.

title: Proverbs 31:15
text: 15. She diligently attends to expending as well as gathering wealth;

title: Proverbs 31:16
text: 16. and hence has means to purchase property.

title: Proverbs 31:17
text: 17, 18. To energy she adds a watchfulness in bargains, and a protracted and painful industry. The last clause may figuratively denote that her prosperity (compare  Proverbs 24:20 ) is not short lived.

title: Proverbs 31:19
text: 19. No work, however mean, if honest, is disdained.

title: Proverbs 31:20
text: 20. Industry enables her to be charitable.

title: Proverbs 31:21
text: 21. scarlet--or, "purple," by reason of the dyes used, the best fabrics; as a matter of taste also; the color suits cold.

title: Proverbs 31:22
text:
22. coverings of tapestry--or, "coverlets," that is, for beds. 
 
    silk--or, "linen" (compare  Exodus 26:1 Exodus 27:9 ) 
 
    and purple--that is, the most costly goods.

title: Proverbs 31:23
text: 23. in the gates--(compare  Proverbs 22:22 ). His domestic comfort promotes his advancement in public dignity.

title: Proverbs 31:24
text:
24. fine linen--or, "linen shirts," or the material for them. 
 
    girdles--were often costly and highly valued ( II Samuel 18:11 ). 
 
    delivereth--or, "giveth as a present" or "to sell."

title: Proverbs 31:25
text:
25. Strength and honour--Strong and beautiful is her clothing; or, figuratively, for moral character, vigorous and honorable. 
 
    shall rejoice ... come--in confidence of certain maintenance.

title: Proverbs 31:26
text: 26. Her conversation is wise and gentle.

title: Proverbs 31:27
text: 27. (Compare  I Timothy 5:14 Titus 2:5 ). She adds to her example a wise management of those under her control.

title: Proverbs 31:28
text: 28. She is honored by those who best know her.

title: Proverbs 31:29
text:
29. The words are those of her husband, praising her. 
 
    virtuously--(Compare  Proverbs 31:10 ).

title: Proverbs 31:30
text:
30. Favour--or, "Grace" of personal manner. 
 
    beauty--of face, or form (compare  Proverbs 11:22 ). True piety alone commands permanent respect and affection ( I Peter 3:3 ).

title: Proverbs 31:31
text: 31. The result of her labor is her best eulogy. Nothing can add to the simple beauty of this admirable portrait. On the measure of its realization in the daughters of our own day rest untold results, in the domestic, and, therefore, the civil and religious, welfare of the people.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:1
text:
Ecclesiastes 1:1-18 . INTRODUCTION. 
 
    1. the Preacher--and Convener of assemblies for the purpose. See my (unresolved link). Koheleth in Hebrew, a symbolical name for Solomon, and of Heavenly Wisdom speaking through and identified with him.  Ecclesiastes 1:12  shows that "king of Jerusalem" is in apposition, not with "David," but "Preacher." 
 
    of Jerusalem--rather, "in Jerusalem," for it was merely his metropolis, not his whole kingdom.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:2
text:
2. The theme proposed of the first part of his discourse. 
 
    Vanity of vanities--Hebraism for the most utter vanity. So "holy of holies" ( Exodus 26:33 ); "servant of servants" ( Genesis 9:25 ). The repetition increases the force. 
 
    all--Hebrew, "the all"; all without exception, namely, earthly things. 
 
    vanity--not in themselves, for God maketh nothing in vain ( I Timothy 4:4 I Timothy 4:5 ), but vain when put in the place of God and made the end, instead of the means ( Psalms 39:5 Psalms 39:6 Psalms 62:9 Matthew 6:33 ); vain, also, because of the "vanity" to which they are "subjected" by the fall ( Romans 8:20 ).

title: Ecclesiastes 1:3
text:
3. What profit ... labour--that is, "What profit" as to the chief good ( Matthew 16:26 ). Labor is profitable in its proper place ( Genesis 2:15 Genesis 3:19 Proverbs 14:23 ). 
 
    under the sun--that is, in this life, as opposed to the future world. The phrase often recurs, but only in Ecclesiastes.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:4
text: 4. earth ... for ever-- ( Psalms 104:5 ). While the earth remains the same, the generations of men are ever changing; what lasting profit, then, can there be from the toils of one whose sojourn on earth, as an individual, is so brief? The "for ever" is comparative, not absolute ( Psalms 102:26 ).

title: Ecclesiastes 1:5
text: 5. ( Psalms 19:5 Psalms 19:6 ). "Panting" as the Hebrew for "hasteth"; metaphor, from a runner ( Psalms 19:5 , "a strong man") in a "race." It applies rather to the rising sun, which seems laboriously to mount up to the meridian, than to the setting sun; the accents too favor MAURER, "And (that too, returning) to his place, where panting he riseth."

title: Ecclesiastes 1:6
text: 6. according to his circuits--that is, it returns afresh to its former circuits, however many be its previous veerings about. The north and south winds are the two prevailing winds in Palestine and Egypt.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:7
text: 7. By subterraneous cavities, and by evaporation forming rain clouds, the fountains and rivers are supplied from the sea, into which they then flow back. The connection is: Individual men are continually changing, while the succession of the race continues; just as the sun, wind, and rivers are ever shifting about, while the cycle in which they move is invariable; they return to the point whence they set out. Hence is man, as in these objects of nature which are his analogue, with all the seeming changes "there is no new thing" ( Ecclesiastes 1:9 ).

title: Ecclesiastes 1:8
text: 8. MAURER translates, "All words are wearied out," that is, are inadequate, as also, "man cannot express" all the things in the world which undergo this ceaseless, changeless cycle of vicissitudes: "The eye is not satisfied with seeing them," &c. But it is plainly a return to the idea ( Ecclesiastes 1:3 ) as to man's "labor," which is only wearisome and profitless; "no new" good can accrue from it ( Ecclesiastes 1:9 ); for as the sun, &c., so man's laborious works move in a changeless cycle. The eye and ear are two of the taskmasters for which man toils. But these are never "satisfied" ( Ecclesiastes 6:7 Proverbs 27:20 ). Nor can they be so hereafter, for there will be nothing "new." Not so the chief good, Jesus Christ ( John 4:13 John 4:14 Revelation of John 21:5 ).

title: Ecclesiastes 1:9
text: 9. Rather, "no new thing at all"; as in  Numbers 11:6 . This is not meant in a general sense; but there is no new source of happiness (the subject in question) which can be devised; the same round of petty pleasures, cares, business, study, wars, &c., being repeated over and over again [HOLDEN].

title: Ecclesiastes 1:10
text:
10. old time--Hebrew, "ages." 
 
    which was--The Hebrew plural cannot be joined to the verb singular. Therefore translate: "It hath been in the ages before; certainly it hath been before us" [HOLDEN].
